explanation: When physically disposed, the inventory and its associated provision are both removed. If no provision exists, the full cost is expensed directly to Inventory Loss Expense.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Dead stock write-offs require both a physical disposal event and an accounting entry. In the ERP, close out the inventory location for the disposed items and post the write-off against the existing Allowance for Slow-Moving Inventory. If the write-off exceeds the provision (i.e., items without a prior provision), the excess is expensed directly to Inventory Loss Expense. For tax purposes in Jordan, disposal evidence is required to support the deduction.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors require physical disposal evidence: (1) Destruction certificate (for products that cannot be donated or returned), donation receipt (for items given to charity), or liquidation invoice (for items sold below cost). Writing off inventory without physical disposal evidence is a significant audit finding — the items may still exist and could be misappropriated.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Disposal authorization signed by management, physical disposal evidence (destruction certificate, donation acknowledgment, or liquidation sale invoice), write-off journal entry linked to the specific inventory items, prior provision balance confirming the allowance was available to absorb the write-off, and ISTD guidance on tax deductibility of inventory write-offs in Jordan.

title: How to Record Inbound Consignment Stock Received from a Vendor
description: Tracking inventory received on consignment without recording it as the store's own asset.
explanation: Consignment stock is NOT your asset — you hold it on behalf of the vendor. It is tracked in a memo or off-balance-sheet account. No purchase is recorded until a sale occurs.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure consignment vendor locations in your WMS as non-owned inventory zones. The system should track quantity, SKU, and value for warehouse management purposes without including consignment stock in the financial inventory balance. Use a memo ledger or a separate entity/dimension in the ERP for consignment tracking. Conduct regular reconciliation of consignment stock on hand against the vendor's records.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Consignment inventory appearing on the balance sheet is an overstatement of assets and liabilities. Auditors test: (1) Does the store's inventory balance include any goods not owned (consignment, customer-owned repair stock, goods on approval)? (2) Is the consignment agreement clearly documented, confirming title remains with the vendor until sale? (3) Is consignment stock adequately insured even though it is not owned?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Consignment agreement with vendor (title retention clause, commission rate, reporting obligations, return conditions), inbound consignment receipt (SKU, quantity, vendor valuation), regular consignment stock count report reconciled to vendor records, and insurance coverage confirmation for consignment stock.

title: How to Record a Consignment Sale and Vendor Payout
description: Recognizing only the commission as revenue when a consignment item sells and clearing the memo stock.
explanation: When the item sells, only the store's commission is revenue. The vendor's share is a liability. The consignment memo account is also cleared at this point.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: When a consignment item sells, two things happen simultaneously: (1) The memo consignment stock is reduced (warehouse management), and (2) The financial entries are posted (cash in, vendor payable, commission revenue). Automate the linkage in your OMS so that a consignment sale triggers both events. Generate monthly consignment sales reports to vendors detailing items sold, dates, and amounts owed.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: The principal vs. agent distinction governs the revenue amount: only the commission is recorded, not the full sale price. Auditors test: (1) Gross revenue booking of consignment sales (a common error that overstates revenue), (2) Timely settlement of vendor payables — aging consignment payables may indicate a dispute or cash flow issue, (3) Memo stock balance reconciles to vendor confirmations.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Consignment sales report (by vendor, SKU, sale date, sale price, commission rate, amount due to vendor), vendor remittance statement and payment confirmation, memo consignment stock movement records, and monthly reconciliation of Payable to Consignor balance.

title: How to Record Revenue and COGS for a Dropshipping Order
description: Accounting for a dropshipped sale where the supplier ships directly to the customer — no inventory is held.
explanation: In dropshipping, inventory is never held. When an order is placed, the cost owed to the supplier is recognized immediately as COGS. There is no inventory asset at any point.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Dropship orders require a virtual PO raised against the supplier at the time of customer order. The ERP posts COGS and Accounts Payable when the supplier confirms dispatch. No inventory account is touched. Track dropship orders in a separate product category so that dropship COGS (and its higher variability due to spot supplier pricing) is distinguishable from owned-inventory COGS in the P&L.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify: (1) Revenue recognition timing — revenue should be recognized at customer delivery, not supplier dispatch, (2) COGS accuracy — dropship supplier costs fluctuate more than fixed-inventory costs; test that actual supplier invoices match the COGS posted, (3) Principal vs. agent analysis — are you controlling the goods (principal) or merely facilitating (agent)?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Customer order confirmation, supplier dispatch confirmation with tracking number, supplier invoice (for COGS verification), customer delivery confirmation, payment gateway receipt for customer payment, and accounts payable record for supplier settlement.

title: How to Record a Kitting or Bundling Assembly in the Warehouse
description: Reclassifying individual product components into a new bundle SKU when assembling kits in the warehouse.
explanation: Kitting transfers the cost of individual components into a new bundle SKU. The total inventory value remains unchanged — it is simply reclassified from component items to a bundle item.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set up a Bill of Materials (BOM) in the ERP for each bundle SKU, listing the component items and quantities. When the kitting work order is completed in the WMS, the ERP automatically relieves the component inventory and increases the bundle SKU inventory. Any assembly labor or packaging costs added during kitting should be included in the bundle cost. Maintain traceability from bundle back to components for cost accuracy.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Kitting entries are internal inventory transfers — no expense should be recognized unless assembly labor or consumables are incurred. Auditors test: (1) Component inventory is fully relieved when bundles are built — no double-counting of components and bundles, (2) Bundle cost equals the sum of component costs plus any additional assembly costs, (3) Disassembled kits (un-kitting) correctly reverse the entry and restore component inventory.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Bill of Materials per bundle SKU, kitting work order (components consumed, bundle units produced, assembly date), updated inventory movement report confirming component relief and bundle creation, assembly labor cost allocation (if applicable), and cycle count confirmation of bundle SKUs.

title: How to Record Outbound Shipping Costs for Customer Orders
description: Expensing the courier charge for delivering a customer order as a selling and fulfillment cost.
explanation: Outbound shipping costs are a selling expense. They are tracked separately from COGS to analyze total fulfillment cost and whether free shipping promotions are economically viable.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Integrate your courier accounts (Aramex, DHL, local carriers) with the ERP so that each order's shipping label cost is posted automatically to Shipping & Fulfillment Expense. Track cost per shipment to enable cost-per-order analysis. Segment by shipping zone (domestic/international) and weight tier for rate card compliance. Free shipping promotions should show the full cost in this expense account — do not net against revenue.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Shipping costs can be material for e-commerce businesses. Auditors check: (1) All outbound shipments have a corresponding expense — courier invoices are reconciled to shipment volumes, (2) Shipping costs are not capitalized into inventory (they are a period cost for outbound fulfillment), (3) The courier rate card used for accruals matches the signed agreement.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Courier invoice or account statement (per-shipment billing detail), signed courier rate card, monthly shipping cost per order analysis, and reconciliation of shipped orders to courier billing records.

title: How to Record Shipping Fees Charged to Customers
description: Recognizing shipping revenue when a customer pays for express or standard delivery at checkout.
explanation: When customers pay for shipping, it is recognized as a separate revenue stream. This helps the store measure whether shipping fees cover the actual courier costs.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure shipping fee line items as a distinct product/service code in your OMS so they post to a Shipping Revenue account separate from product Sales Revenue. This enables a true shipping P&L: shipping fee revenue vs. actual courier cost. For VAT purposes in Jordan, shipping fees charged to customers may be taxable — verify applicable tax treatment based on the nature of the shipped goods.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors assess whether shipping revenue is recognized at the right time: (1) Revenue should be recognized when the shipping service is rendered (delivery), not when the fee is collected at checkout, (2) For undelivered orders at period-end, the shipping fee collected should be deferred along with the product revenue, (3) Shipping fee VAT treatment should be consistent — charged if the underlying goods are taxable.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: OMS order detail showing shipping fee per order, monthly shipping revenue report, courier cost report for same period (to calculate shipping margin), VAT treatment documentation for shipping fees, and shipping fee refund log (for cancelled orders).

title: How to Record a Third-Party Logistics (3PL) Monthly Service Fee
description: Accounting for the monthly invoice from a 3PL warehouse covering storage, pick-and-pack, and fulfillment services.
explanation: 3PL costs replace the need for owned warehouse space and staff. They are a key variable cost that scales with order volume and are tracked as part of the total fulfilment cost per order.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: 3PL invoices typically contain multiple line items: storage (per pallet/sqm), pick-and-pack (per order), receiving (per inbound shipment), and special handling fees. Map each line item to a distinct sub-account within Fulfilment Expense for cost visibility. Accrue the 3PL fee at month-end if the invoice arrives after the close — use the 3PL's provisional report or prior-month actuals as the basis.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: 3PL fees should be reconciled to the service level agreement: (1) Verify storage charges against average pallet positions held in the period, (2) Verify pick-and-pack fees against order volumes from the OMS, (3) Unexpected 'special handling' or 'deviation' fees should be investigated and approved, (4) Check for automatic price escalation clauses in the 3PL contract that may have triggered without notice.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: 3PL monthly service invoice with line-item breakdown, 3PL contract with rate schedule, order volume report from OMS (for pick-and-pack verification), storage utilization report from 3PL (for storage fee verification), and accrual calculation if the invoice is received after month-end.

title: How to Record Warehouse Storage Fees Charged Per Pallet or Square Metre
description: Accounting for monthly charges from a third-party warehouse based on inventory space consumed.
explanation: Storage fees are a direct cost of holding inventory. High storage costs on slow-moving inventory are a key signal that the product mix needs to be optimized.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Track storage fees as part of the holding cost of inventory. High storage costs on slow-moving SKUs may make it economically rational to write down or liquidate those items — the storage fee per month may exceed the margin on eventual sale. Some businesses allocate storage fees to individual SKUs as an additional inventory holding cost, though this is complex to implement and not required under IAS 2.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Storage fees are relatively straightforward but auditors verify: (1) The rate per pallet/sqm matches the warehouse contract, (2) Charges are accrued in the period the space is occupied — not just when the invoice arrives, (3) Storage of obsolete or dead stock (which should have been written off) is not generating ongoing fees without impairment recognition.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Warehouse contract with storage rate schedule, monthly storage utilization report (pallet/sqm used), storage fee invoice, and cross-reference of high-cost storage SKUs to the slow-moving inventory report.

title: How to Record Per-Order Pick-and-Pack Fees from a 3PL
description: Expensing the handling fee charged by a 3PL for picking, packing, and preparing each customer order for dispatch.
explanation: Pick-and-pack fees are variable costs scaling with order volume. Tracking this separately from storage allows accurate calculation of the cost-to-serve per order.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Calculate total pick-and-pack fees by multiplying the contracted rate per order by the number of orders dispatched in the period. Use OMS order export data to verify the volume independently from the 3PL's invoice. Track pick-and-pack cost per order as a KPI — typically JOD 1.50–4.00 per order depending on complexity. Multi-item orders with custom packaging cost more.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Verify the 3PL's pick-and-pack invoice against OMS dispatch records: order count and SKU complexity should reconcile. Check that special handling surcharges (fragile items, oversized products) are consistent with the product types shipped. Automated reconciliation reduces error risk significantly.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: 3PL pick-and-pack invoice (with per-order detail or order volume summary), OMS dispatch count for the same period, rate card from 3PL contract, variance analysis (invoiced orders vs. OMS orders), and cost-per-order trend report.

title: How to Record a Prepaid Shipping Label Credit Top-Up
description: Treating a bulk top-up to a courier shipping account as a prepaid asset, expensed as labels are consumed.
explanation: Bulk top-ups to a courier account are prepaid assets. The balance is expensed as labels are consumed for each shipment, ensuring the cost is matched to the orders it relates to.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain a Prepaid Shipping Credits account in the ERP linked to each courier account balance. When labels are purchased (credits consumed), the system should automatically debit Shipping & Fulfillment Expense and credit Prepaid Shipping Credits. Reconcile the ERP prepaid balance to the courier portal balance at month-end. Any unused balance at period-end remains as a prepaid asset.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Prepaid shipping credits are straightforward but auditors will verify: (1) The ERP balance matches the actual courier account balance at reporting date, (2) Credits are being consumed and expensed as shipments are made — not left on the balance sheet indefinitely, (3) Courier account access is controlled to prevent unauthorized use of prepaid credits.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Courier account top-up confirmation, courier portal balance statement at month-end, label consumption report (labels generated per period with cost per label), prepaid balance reconciliation (ERP vs. courier portal), and courier account access controls documentation.

title: How to Record Return Shipping Costs Absorbed by the Store
description: Accounting for the cost of prepaid return labels provided to customers as a cost of the returns policy.
explanation: Free returns are a customer retention tool but a real cost. Tracking return shipping separately enables the business to measure the true cost of its returns policy.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Create return shipment label costs as a separate expense code from outbound shipping so the total cost of returns can be measured. The true cost of a return is: outbound shipping + return shipping + restocking labor + any inventory value loss — all of which should be trackable at the order level for high-value returns.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Return shipping costs are often understated because they flow through the prepaid credits account without explicit expense tracking. Auditors test: (1) Are all issued return labels matched to actual return shipments? (2) Is the cost of unexercised (issued but unused) return labels expensed or left as prepaid? Issued labels not yet used should remain as prepaid until the return is confirmed.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Return label issuance log (label ID, order reference, customer, issuance date, cost), return receipt confirmation from courier (confirming the label was used), updated prepaid credits balance, and monthly returns cost analysis (return rate × average return label cost).

title: How to Record a Delivery Damage Claim Against a Courier
description: Setting up the insurance or damage claim receivable when a courier confirms liability for goods damaged in transit.
explanation: When a courier damages goods in transit and accepts liability, the claim receivable offsets the inventory loss previously recorded. The claim is recognized when the courier confirms acceptance.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain a Damage Claims sub-ledger tracking: claim reference, courier, order ID, claimed amount, status (submitted/accepted/rejected/settled), and payment date. Only recognize the receivable when the courier formally accepts liability — not when the claim is submitted, as recovery is not certain until acceptance. Close out the receivable to Cash when payment is received.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Damage claim receivables are tested for recoverability: (1) Are only accepted (not merely submitted) claims on the balance sheet? (2) Are claims supported by courier acknowledgment documentation? (3) Are long-outstanding claims (90+ days after acceptance) reviewed for collectability? (4) Claims for amounts exceeding the courier's declared liability limit may not be fully recoverable.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Damage claim submission (photos of damaged goods, courier tracking reference, claimed amount), courier's written acceptance of liability, claim settlement correspondence, payment receipt, and reconciliation of Damage Claims receivable to courier claims register.

title: How to Record a Customer Return When the Product Is Restocked
description: Reversing both revenue and COGS and returning the item to inventory when a clean return is received.
explanation: A clean return reverses both the revenue and the COGS. The product re-enters inventory at its original cost. Using Sales Returns (not a direct debit to Revenue) allows tracking of return volume as a KPI.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The return workflow in the OMS should: (1) Issue a Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA), (2) Receive the item back in the WMS, (3) Inspection — if the item passes quality check, trigger the inventory reinstatement and COGS reversal, (4) Process the refund to the customer. These steps must flow through the ERP in the correct sequence — inventory should not be restocked before quality inspection.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Returns are a high-risk area for revenue manipulation and fraud: (1) Returns recorded without a corresponding inbound physical receipt — fictitious returns, (2) Items restocked that should have been rejected (damaged) — inventory overstatement, (3) Large return volumes from a single customer or channel — potential return fraud, (4) COGS reversal at a cost different from the original sale cost — inventory valuation error.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: RMA authorization, return shipping receipt (customer-side dispatch and merchant-side receipt), quality inspection report (condition confirmed as resellable), refund confirmation, WMS inventory receipt record, and original sales order reference for COGS reversal at correct cost.

title: How to Record a Customer Return When the Damaged Product Cannot Be Restocked
description: Processing a return where the customer receives a refund but the returned item is unsellable and must be expensed.
explanation: Revenue is reversed but the product cannot go back into inventory. COGS is also reversed, but the cost of the damaged item is recognized as an Inventory Loss expense — the net effect is still a loss on the order.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: When an inspection fails, the WMS should route the item to a 'Damaged Returns' bin, which triggers the Inventory Loss entry rather than the inventory reinstatement. Document the inspection outcome in the RMA record. Analyze Inventory Loss — Returns by category and root cause: customer misuse, transit damage, or product defect. High product-defect rates may trigger supplier claims.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test the completeness of Inventory Loss — Returns: (1) Are all failed inspections recorded as losses? (2) Are damaged items physically destroyed or disposed of — not sitting in a damaged bin indefinitely, (3) For high-frequency damage from a specific courier, has a damage claim been raised? (4) Is the loss value based on the original cost (correct) or retail price (incorrect)?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: RMA and quality inspection report (inspection outcome — failed, reason for failure), damaged item disposal record, Inventory Loss entry linked to the failed inspection, refund confirmation, and supplier claim documentation if the damage is attributable to a product defect.

title: How to Record a Partial Refund or Goodwill Allowance to a Customer
description: Issuing a partial cash refund to a customer who keeps a slightly damaged item — without reversing the full sale.
explanation: A partial refund does not reverse the full sale or the COGS — the customer keeps the product. Only the refunded amount reduces revenue as a Sales Allowance.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Partial refunds should be tracked separately from full returns in your OMS and ERP. Use a Sales Allowances account (distinct from Sales Returns) so that management reporting shows: full returns separately from partial goodwill adjustments. This allows better understanding of the customer service cost of minor quality issues resolved without a full return.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Goodwill allowances are a potential earnings management tool — large or unusual allowances near period-end should be scrutinized. Auditors verify: (1) Allowances are supported by customer communications or complaint records, (2) The allowance amount is proportionate to the issue described, (3) Allowances are not being used to accelerate expense recognition or reduce reported revenue inappropriately.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Customer complaint or support ticket documenting the issue, refund approval in the customer service system, partial refund amount calculation, bank transfer or gateway refund confirmation, and monthly Sales Allowances report by reason code.

title: How to Record a Marketplace-Initiated Refund from Noon or Amazon
description: Accounting for automatic customer refunds issued by the marketplace and charged back to the merchant.
explanation: Marketplaces often issue refunds directly to customers and deduct the amount from the merchant's next settlement. The deduction reduces the marketplace receivable balance.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Marketplace-initiated refunds appear on the settlement statement as deductions. When importing the settlement, parse refund line items separately from commission deductions and record each as a Sales Returns & Allowances entry reducing the marketplace receivable. Track refund rates by marketplace to compare return behavior across channels.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Marketplace refunds are outside the merchant's direct control — auditors verify: (1) All refund deductions on settlement statements are recorded as Sales Returns, (2) Refunds for items that were restocked also trigger COGS reversal and inventory reinstatement entries, (3) High refund rates on a specific marketplace may indicate a listing quality or product issue warranting disclosure.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Marketplace settlement statement showing refund line items (order ID, refund amount, reason code), product inventory return status (restocked vs. not returned), Sales Returns reconciliation to marketplace settlement, and monthly marketplace-level refund rate report.

title: How to Record a COD Order Rejected and Returned at the Door
description: Reversing all entries when a COD customer refuses to accept delivery and the order is sent back.
explanation: If a COD customer refuses the parcel, the courier returns it. Revenue and COGS are both reversed and inventory is restocked. The courier receivable that was set up at dispatch is also cleared.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: COD rejections are extremely common in MENA markets — rejection rates of 20–40% are not unusual. Configure your OMS to automatically trigger the full reversal when the courier updates the delivery status to 'Rejected' or 'RTS (Return to Sender)'. The reversal should happen in the same accounting period as the original dispatch entry when possible to avoid period-end distortions.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: COD rejection rates are a key audit metric for MENA e-commerce: (1) High unrecorded COD returns will overstate both revenue and the Receivable: Courier balance, (2) Courier return confirmations must be obtained before reversing — items marked returned that are still in transit should stay on the courier receivable, (3) Repeated rejections from the same address may indicate a fraudulent order pattern.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Courier rejection notification (order ID, rejection date, reason code), return-to-sender confirmation with tracking, quality inspection of returned item, inventory reinstatement record in WMS, and monthly COD rejection rate report by courier and geography.

title: How to Record a HyperPay or PayTabs Weekly Settlement
description: Clearing the payment gateway receivable and recognizing processing fees when a regional gateway remits collected funds.
explanation: Regional payment gateways like HyperPay and PayTabs hold collected funds and settle weekly. The gross receivable is cleared, the fee is expensed, and the net cash hits the bank.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Treat regional gateways (HyperPay, PayTabs, Telr) identically to Stripe — maintain a dedicated Receivable: Gateway account per provider. Gross sales are posted to the receivable at transaction time; fees and net cash are recorded at settlement. Reconcile the gateway receivable balance to the gateway's merchant dashboard at each reporting date.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Regional gateways may have less mature reconciliation tools than global providers — manual reconciliation is often required. Auditors test: (1) Gateway receivable balance agrees to the provider's outstanding balance report, (2) Fee rates applied in settlements match the signed gateway agreement, (3) Settlement delays beyond the contract SLA are investigated and disclosed if material.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Gateway settlement statement (transaction-level detail, fees, net payout), bank deposit confirmation, gateway merchant dashboard balance at reporting date, signed gateway agreement with fee schedule, and monthly receivable reconciliation schedule.

title: How to Reconcile and Record a PayPal Balance Withdrawal to Your Bank
description: Recording the transfer of accumulated PayPal balance to the main operating bank account.
explanation: The PayPal balance is a separate asset account. When funds are withdrawn to the bank, it is a transfer between asset accounts — not a revenue event. Revenue was recognized at the time of each sale.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain PayPal as a separate bank/cash account in the ERP chart of accounts. Individual PayPal transactions (sales, refunds, fees) should be imported and posted in real time or via daily batch. Withdrawals to the bank account are simple internal transfers — debit Main Bank, credit PayPal Balance. The PayPal account balance in the ERP must reconcile to the PayPal account statement at month-end.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: A common error is treating PayPal withdrawals as income — this double-counts revenue already recognized at sale. Auditors reconcile the PayPal account: (1) Opening balance + sales − refunds − fees − withdrawals = closing balance, (2) Closing balance ties to PayPal statement, (3) Any PayPal holds or reserves are reclassified to Restricted Cash.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: PayPal monthly account statement, bank deposit confirmation for each withdrawal, PayPal account reconciliation (transaction-level), and any PayPal reserves or holds documentation.

title: How to Record a Bank Currency Conversion Fee on USD to JOD
description: Accounting for the bank's spread or fee when converting USD e-commerce proceeds to Jordanian dinars.
explanation: International e-commerce stores collecting USD must convert to local currency for operations. The conversion spread or fixed fee is a finance cost, not a revenue reduction.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set up multi-currency in the ERP with USD and JOD accounts. USD-denominated gateway receivables are recorded at the transaction date rate. At conversion, the JOD received plus FX fee are recorded, and any remaining difference between the original JOD equivalent (at transaction rate) and the actual JOD received is an FX gain/loss. The bank's conversion fee is a separate finance cost.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: FX conversion accounting requires precision: (1) Is the rate used for initial USD entry the actual transaction date rate or a standard rate? (2) Is the FX fee segregated from the FX gain/loss — they are economically similar but may be classified differently (fee = finance cost, gain/loss = other income/expense), (3) At year-end, USD balances remaining unconverted must be retranslated at the closing rate.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Bank conversion confirmation (USD amount converted, rate applied, JOD received, fee charged), transaction date rate documentation (Central Bank of Jordan rate or bank's published rate), FX gain/loss calculation, and monthly FX conversion summary.

title: How to Record a Payment Gateway Reserve or Dispute Hold
description: Reclassifying gateway-held funds as restricted cash when a rolling reserve is imposed due to chargeback risk.
explanation: Payment gateways may hold a rolling reserve (typically 5-10% of volume for 90 days) for merchants with elevated chargeback risk. This is still the merchant's money — reclassified as restricted cash.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Track gateway reserves in a dedicated Restricted Cash account. The reserve is the merchant's asset but is not freely available — it should be classified as current or non-current based on the expected release date (rolling 90-day reserves are typically current). As the reserve releases monthly (after 90 days), reclassify from Restricted Cash back to the gateway balance or directly to Cash in Bank.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors assess whether gateway reserves are properly disclosed: (1) Restricted cash should be separately disclosed from unrestricted cash on the balance sheet, (2) Reserves subject to dispute outcomes (not just time-based rolling reserves) may require disclosure as contingent liabilities, (3) If a reserve is growing rapidly, it may signal worsening chargeback rates — a business health indicator.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Gateway reserve confirmation letter or dashboard statement (reserve amount, basis, release schedule), restricted cash schedule (opening balance, additions, releases, closing balance), and cash flow statement classification (restricted cash excluded from cash and cash equivalents).

title: How to Reverse a Failed Card Payment After Initial Authorization
description: Voiding a sale entry when a payment authorization fails after the initial transaction is recorded.
explanation: If a payment is initially authorized but subsequently fails (insufficient funds, fraud detection), the revenue entry must be reversed. The order is cancelled and inventory is not released.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Payment gateways typically do not settle failed authorizations — the charge reverses automatically within 24–72 hours. The ERP should match incoming gateway reversal events to the original transaction and auto-reverse the revenue entry. Ensure that inventory was not already dispatched for the failed payment — inventory released before payment confirmation is a fulfillment controls failure.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Failed payment reversals should net to zero — the revenue entry and its reversal cancel out. Auditors check: (1) No inventory was released for failed payments, (2) Failed payment reversal entries are matched 1:1 to the original transaction — no orphaned reversals without an original entry, (3) High rates of late payment failures (authorized, dispatched, then reversed) indicate a weak pre-payment verification process.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Gateway decline notification (with transaction ID, decline reason code), reversal confirmation from gateway, original authorization record, order cancellation confirmation in OMS, and inventory hold release record (confirming stock was not dispatched).

title: How to Record an In-House Customer Instalment Plan Receivable
description: Recognizing full revenue at point of sale and splitting the receivable between current and long-term portions for own-funded instalment plans.
explanation: When the store itself offers instalment plans, full revenue is recognized at point of sale (control has passed). The receivable is split between current (due in 12 months) and long-term portions.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain an instalment schedule sub-ledger per customer showing: due dates, instalment amounts, payments received, and outstanding balance. The current/long-term split must be updated at each reporting date as time passes and instalments fall due. Apply the effective interest method if the instalments contain a significant financing component (IFRS 15 / IAS 32 interaction).
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: In-house instalment receivables carry credit risk — auditors assess: (1) Is a provision for doubtful instalments maintained based on delinquency experience? (2) Has the financing component been assessed — if instalments extend beyond 12 months, does the interest element need to be separated? (3) Is the current/long-term classification updated at each reporting date?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Customer instalment agreement (schedule, amounts, due dates, late payment terms), instalment sub-ledger per customer, payment receipt records, impairment provision calculation, and reclassification schedule (moving long-term to current as instalments come due within 12 months).

title: How to Release Monthly Ad Spend from a Prepaid Advertising Balance
description: Amortizing one month's portion of a prepaid advertising campaign from asset to expense.
explanation: A prepaid ad campaign is released to expense each month as the ads run. This matches the cost to the revenue it generates in each period.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set up a recurring auto-journal in the ERP at the campaign start date that automatically releases the monthly allocation from Prepaid Advertising to Marketing Expense. If the campaign performs ahead of schedule (all budget consumed before the planned end date), accelerate the expense recognition to match actual ad delivery. Reconcile the Prepaid Advertising balance monthly to confirm no unrecognized amounts remain after campaign end.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Period-end prepaid advertising balances are tested for: (1) Active campaigns supporting the prepaid balance — expired campaigns should be fully expensed, (2) Monthly release amounts tied to campaign delivery reports, not just time elapsed, (3) Cancelled campaigns triggering immediate expense recognition (or refund if unused balance is recoverable).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Campaign booking confirmation (dates, total value, monthly breakdown), amortization schedule, monthly campaign delivery report (confirming ads ran), platform invoice or deduction statement, and cancellation/refund policy documentation.

title: How to Record a Google Shopping or Performance Max Campaign Invoice
description: Expensing a monthly Google Ads invoice for product listing and performance campaigns.
explanation: Pay-per-click and shopping campaign costs are expensed in the month the ads ran. Tracking Google Ads spend separately from social media spend enables channel-level ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) analysis.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Google Ads invoices are issued monthly (or when the account threshold is reached for auto-billing accounts). Map Google Ads charges to the correct cost center and campaign type (Shopping, Performance Max, Search) to enable channel-level ROAS analysis. For VAT purposes in Jordan, apply the reverse charge mechanism on Google Ads invoices from a foreign entity.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Google Ads spend should be matched to campaign delivery data: (1) Invoice amount reconciled to Google Ads account billing summary, (2) Reverse charge VAT self-assessed on the foreign service invoice, (3) If accruing for ads delivered but not yet invoiced at period-end, use the Google Ads account's cost report as the accrual basis.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Google Ads invoice, Google Ads account billing summary (campaign-level spend), credit card statement or payment confirmation, VAT reverse charge self-assessment record, and monthly ROAS report by campaign type.

title: How to Record a Monthly SMS and Email Marketing Platform Subscription
description: Expensing recurring subscriptions to marketing automation tools like Klaviyo or Mailchimp.
explanation: Email and SMS marketing tools are recurring operating costs. They are expensed monthly as a selling & marketing expense.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Marketing tool subscriptions (Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Brevo) are typically billed monthly or annually. Monthly billing is expensed directly. Annual prepayments should be capitalized as Prepaid Technology Subscriptions and amortized monthly. Track separately from one-off campaign spend to understand fixed marketing infrastructure costs vs. variable campaign costs.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Subscriptions are low-risk but auditors verify: (1) Annual subscriptions are amortized, not expensed in full at payment, (2) Subscriptions for platforms no longer in use are cancelled and any prepaid balance refunded or written off, (3) The subscription tier charged matches the company's current contact list size — overpaying for unused capacity is a minor inefficiency worth flagging.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Platform subscription invoice or billing confirmation, credit card statement or bank transfer record, and for annual subscriptions, the prepaid amortization schedule.

title: How to Defer Revenue When Customers Earn Loyalty Points at Purchase
description: Splitting sale proceeds between recognized revenue and a deferred loyalty points liability under IFRS 15.
explanation: Under IFRS 15, loyalty points that customers can redeem are a separate performance obligation. The estimated redemption value (5% of sale) is deferred as a liability until points are used or expire.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure your loyalty program integration to pass the points earned per transaction to the ERP alongside the sale entry. The deferred amount should reflect the stand-alone selling price of the points — typically the expected redemption value adjusted for the estimated redemption rate (not all points will be redeemed). Update the Loyalty Points Liability monthly as new points are issued and existing points are redeemed or expire.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Loyalty program accounting under IFRS 15 requires judgment: (1) Is the deferred amount based on the standalone value of points (redemption value × expected redemption rate) or just the face value? (2) Is the redemption rate assumption supported by historical data? (3) Is the liability reconciled monthly to the loyalty platform's outstanding points balance?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Loyalty program terms (points earn rate, redemption value, expiry policy), standalone selling price analysis for loyalty points, historical redemption rate data, monthly loyalty points issuance and redemption report, and Loyalty Points Liability reconciliation.

title: How to Record Loyalty Points Redeemed on a Customer Purchase
description: Converting the loyalty liability to earned revenue when a customer applies accumulated points at checkout.
explanation: The points liability is converted to revenue when redeemed. The customer pays the difference in cash. Full COGS is recognized on the total sale price.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The loyalty redemption transaction should automatically trigger: (1) Reduction of the customer's points balance in the loyalty platform, (2) Reduction of the Loyalty Points Liability in the ERP, (3) Recognition of the full sale revenue (with cash covering the non-points portion), (4) COGS recognition. Ensure the loyalty platform balance and the ERP liability account reconcile — discrepancies arise when points are voided or adjusted manually.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors trace loyalty redemptions from the loyalty platform transaction log to the ERP revenue entries: (1) Revenue recognized must equal the full transaction value, including the points-covered portion, (2) COGS must be based on the full product cost — not reduced because part of the 'payment' was non-cash, (3) Points deducted from the customer's balance must match the Loyalty Points Liability reduction.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Loyalty platform redemption transaction log, order confirmation showing points applied and cash balance, Loyalty Points Liability rollforward (opening balance + earned − redeemed − expired = closing), and COGS report confirming full cost recognition at redemption.

title: How to Record Loyalty Points Breakage from Expired Unredeemed Points
description: Recognizing income from loyalty points that have expired without redemption based on historical expiry patterns.
explanation: Points that expire are an obligation that no longer exists. The liability is released to Other Income. The amount is estimated using historical expiry patterns.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Run the loyalty breakage analysis quarterly using the proportional method: for each points issuance cohort, recognize breakage income as redemptions occur in proportion to the expected total redemption rate. Points with a specific expiry date trigger breakage income when the expiry passes and the points are confirmed as lapsed. Reconcile the breakage recognized to the loyalty platform's expired points report.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Loyalty breakage is an income item that can be used to manage earnings. Auditors test: (1) Is the breakage methodology consistent with IFRS 15 (proportional method or remote method — document which is applied), (2) Is the expected non-redemption rate based on at least 2 years of historical data, (3) Are legal restrictions on expiry being factored in (consumer protection laws in some markets prohibit point expiry)?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Loyalty platform expired points report, breakage methodology memo, historical redemption rate analysis by cohort (minimum 24 months), comparison of estimated breakage to actual expiry, and legal review confirming points expiry is permitted under applicable consumer protection regulations in Jordan.

title: How to Record Flash Sale and Promotional Discount Revenue During Black Friday or Eid
description: Separately tracking promotional price reductions as contra-revenue to preserve the gross revenue figure for analysis.
explanation: Recording the full price and a promotional discount separately preserves the gross revenue figure for performance analysis. Management can see that JOD 39.60 per unit was given away in promotions.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure promotional discount codes in your e-commerce platform to post to a Sales Discounts — Promotional account in the ERP rather than reducing the revenue line directly. This gives management a clear view of gross revenue vs. net revenue, and the total promotional discount budget consumed during a campaign. ROAS calculations using net revenue will understate the platform's driving power — compare gross revenue to ad spend instead.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Large promotional discounts near period-end (Black Friday, Eid) can significantly impact reported revenue. Auditors verify: (1) Discounts are valid promotional codes applied to qualifying transactions, (2) Discount rates are capped per the approved promotion terms, (3) Discount amounts reconcile to the promotional campaign budget approved by management.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Campaign brief and approved discount structure (% or fixed discount, qualifying products, campaign dates), promotion code redemption report (codes used, orders, discount amounts), gross vs. net revenue reconciliation for the campaign period, and management approval for campaign parameters.

title: How to Record a Cash Referral Reward Paid to a Customer
description: Expensing a cash payment made to a referring customer as a customer acquisition cost.
explanation: Cash referral rewards are a customer acquisition cost. They are expensed when paid, not when the referral link was created. They should be tracked against the LTV of referred customers.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Referral rewards can be structured as cash (bank transfer), store credit, or discount codes. Cash rewards are expensed when paid. Store credit rewards create a liability (similar to a gift card) and are expensed when redeemed. Discount code rewards are expensed when the discount is applied to a purchase. Track referral reward spend against the gross margin generated by referred customers to calculate the payback period.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Referral programs are tested for: (1) Rewards paid to fake or self-referral accounts — validate that the referring and referred accounts are distinct, (2) Rewards paid without a confirmed first purchase by the referred customer, (3) Tax treatment — cash payments to customers above a threshold may require withholding tax or 1099-equivalent reporting in some jurisdictions.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Referral program terms (qualifying conditions, reward amount), referral event log (referrer, referred customer, first purchase date, reward triggered date), bank transfer or payment confirmation for cash rewards, and referral ROI analysis (reward cost vs. lifetime value of referred customer cohort).

title: How to Record Monthly Payroll for Warehouse and Fulfillment Staff
description: Accounting for gross wages of warehouse pickers, packers, and receiving staff as a fulfillment cost of revenue.
explanation: Warehouse labor is classified as a Cost of Revenue (fulfilment cost) in e-commerce P&Ls, not a G&A expense. Tracking it separately enables calculation of the total cost-to-fulfill per order.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Payroll for warehouse staff should be allocated to Fulfillment Labor Expense as a Cost of Revenue, distinct from G&A (admin, finance) and S&M (sales, marketing). Use the payroll system's cost center tagging to separate warehouse vs. office vs. customer service headcount. Calculate cost-per-order KPI monthly: total fulfillment labor ÷ orders dispatched.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test: (1) All payroll entries are supported by timesheets or attendance records, (2) Wages paid agree to signed employment contracts or offer letters, (3) Headcount on payroll matches the actual number of active employees (no ghost workers), (4) Cost center allocation is reasonable — warehouse staff coded to G&A would understate cost of revenue and overstate gross margin.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Monthly payroll summary by employee (name, position, gross salary, deductions, net pay), attendance records, employment contracts, cost center allocation schedule, Wages Payable reconciliation, and bank transfer confirmation for net salary payments.

title: How to Record Monthly Payroll for the Customer Service and Returns Team
description: Expensing customer support staff wages — classified as Cost of Revenue or S&M depending on the business model.
explanation: Customer service is either classified as Cost of Revenue or S&M depending on the business model. High return rates increase CS costs significantly — tracking separately enables root cause analysis.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Classify customer service wages consistently — if CS handles post-sale issues (returns, complaints, logistics queries), it is typically Cost of Revenue. If CS is primarily pre-sale (conversion support, product questions), it may qualify as S&M. The classification should be documented in the accounting policy and applied consistently. Track CS cost per ticket and CS cost as a percentage of revenue as operational KPIs.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Misclassification between Cost of Revenue and S&M does not affect total operating expenses but does affect gross margin — a key metric for investors and benchmarking. Auditors verify that the classification is consistent period-to-period and aligned with documented accounting policy.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Payroll summary for CS team, cost center classification rationale (documented in accounting policy), CS ticket volume and resolution rate report, and CS cost-per-ticket analysis.

title: How to Accrue End-of-Service Benefit (EOSB) for Warehouse Staff in Jordan
description: Monthly accrual of the statutory end-of-service indemnity for Jordanian warehouse employees.
explanation: EOSB for warehouse staff is part of the fulfilment cost. It must be accrued monthly to avoid a large unexpected liability when employees leave.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Under the Jordanian Labour Law, EOSB accrues at one month's salary per year of service. The monthly provision = (gross monthly salary ÷ 12) × number of months worked in the year for each employee. Accrue as part of the monthly payroll close process. The Provision for EOSB account should be reconciled to the EOSB sub-ledger (per employee calculation) at each quarter-end.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors recalculate EOSB provisions independently: (1) Is the calculation based on the most recent salary (required — EOSB should reflect the salary at the time of departure, so provisions should be updated when salaries change), (2) Are all eligible employees included — including those on probation for businesses that apply the full law, (3) Has the provision been actuarially reviewed for businesses with large headcounts?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: EOSB calculation schedule by employee (name, start date, current salary, months accrued, provision amount), payroll records confirming current salary, Provision for EOSB reconciliation (opening + monthly accruals − payments for leavers = closing), and Labour Law compliance note confirming applicable EOSB entitlement.

title: How to Record the Employer Social Security Contribution for Operations Staff in Jordan
description: Accruing the employer's 14.25% Social Security Corporation (SSC) contribution on warehouse and operations payroll.
explanation: SSC contributions are part of the true cost of each employee. For warehouse staff, it is a fulfilment cost; for admin staff, it is G&A overhead.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: SSC is calculated on insurable salary (subject to a ceiling). The employer rate is 14.25% and the employee rate is 7.5% (deducted from gross pay). Record both as part of the payroll process: the employer share is an additional expense; the employee share is deducted from gross wages. SSC must be remitted to the Social Security Corporation by the 15th of the following month.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: SSC compliance is tested by the SSC and by auditors: (1) All employees are enrolled — hiring non-registered employees to avoid SSC is illegal, (2) Contributions are calculated on the correct insurable salary (not net of deductions), (3) Remittance is timely — late payments attract penalties, (4) The SSC payable balance clears each month confirming timely payment.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Monthly payroll register with SSC calculation per employee (insurable salary, employer contribution, employee deduction), SSC payment receipt (Form 4), employer contribution reconciliation, and any SSC penalty notices and resolutions.

title: How to Record Packing Materials and Branded Packaging Costs
description: Expensing or capitalizing boxes, bubble wrap, tape, and branded packaging consumed in fulfillment.
explanation: Packaging materials are a direct fulfilment cost. Branded packaging (custom boxes, inserts, tissue paper) can be a significant expense for lifestyle and beauty e-commerce brands.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: High-volume e-commerce businesses should carry packaging supplies as a supplies inventory asset and expense them as consumed (matching principle). Low-volume or startup operations often expense packaging on purchase for simplicity. For branded packaging with long lead times and significant value, the supplies inventory approach provides better cost control. Track cost-per-package as a fulfillment KPI.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Packaging costs are tested for: (1) Significant packaging supplies inventory at year-end — is it properly valued and not overstated? (2) Custom packaging with a logo or branding — is it being expensed as consumed or immediately, and is the treatment consistent? (3) For businesses that capitalize branded packaging as a brand asset — this is not permitted under IAS 38 (it is a consumable, not an intangible).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Packaging supplier invoices (for purchase recording), consumption report from WMS (units of packaging used per period), ending packaging supplies inventory count (if carried as an asset), and cost-per-package calculation.

title: How to Record a Monthly Shopify or WooCommerce Platform Subscription
description: Expensing the recurring monthly fee for the e-commerce store hosting platform.
explanation: E-commerce platform subscriptions are a recurring G&A or technology expense. Unlike infrastructure costs, they are not classified as Cost of Revenue.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Monthly platform fees are expensed directly. Annual Shopify plans paid upfront should be prepaid and amortized monthly. Track platform fees separately from app/plugin fees and transaction fees to understand the full technology cost stack. Shopify transaction fees (for non-Shopify Payments) should be tracked as Payment Processing Fees, not Platform Fees.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Platform subscription fees are low-risk. Auditors check: (1) Annual plans are amortized, not expensed in full at payment, (2) Shopify transaction fees (if applicable) are correctly classified as processing fees rather than platform fees — the distinction matters for gross margin calculation, (3) Unused platform features (e.g., Shopify Plus features not in use) are noted as a cost efficiency opportunity.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Shopify billing history, credit card or bank statement, and for annual plans, the prepaid amortization schedule.

title: How to Record an Annual App or Plugin Subscription for Your Online Store
description: Capitalizing an annual plugin payment as a prepaid asset and amortizing it monthly over the subscription period.
explanation: Annual plugin subscriptions are prepaid assets amortized at JOD 100/month. Multiple small subscriptions for store apps are a growing cost for Shopify-based businesses.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain a prepaid subscriptions schedule in the ERP listing all active annual app subscriptions: name, annual fee, monthly amortization, start date, renewal date. Set up auto-journal entries for monthly amortization to ensure no subscription balance sits on the balance sheet beyond its expiry. Use this schedule proactively to review upcoming renewals and cancel underperforming apps before the renewal date.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Prepaid subscription balances are tested for: (1) All amounts on the prepaid schedule correspond to active, in-use subscriptions, (2) Renewal dates are accurate — amortization period should not extend beyond the renewal/cancellation date, (3) Cancelled subscriptions are written off rather than left to amortize, (4) Refunds received for cancelled subscriptions are recorded as a reduction to the prepaid, not as income.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Annual subscription invoices or receipts per app, prepaid amortization schedule (all active subscriptions with monthly release amounts and renewal dates), cancellation confirmations for any apps discontinued mid-year, and refund receipts where applicable.

title: How to Record Domain Name and SSL Certificate Renewal Costs
description: Expensing annual domain registration and SSL security certificate renewal fees.
explanation: Domain and SSL costs are minor annual expenses typically expensed in the month they are renewed. A multi-year domain registration would be prepaid and amortized.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Single-year domain and SSL renewals are immaterial and can be expensed in the renewal month. Multi-year registrations (e.g., 5-year domain registration) should be prepaid and amortized over the registration period. Maintain a renewals calendar to ensure domain registrations do not lapse — an expired domain can take the entire store offline.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Domain and SSL costs are immaterial for most businesses but: (1) Multi-year prepayments must be amortized, not expensed upfront, (2) Premium domain acquisitions (e.g., purchasing a domain for brand value) may qualify as an intangible asset under IAS 38, (3) SSL certificate lapses resulting in customer security warnings should be noted as a business continuity risk.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Domain registrar renewal invoice, SSL certificate renewal invoice, multi-year registration amortization schedule (if applicable), and domain expiry calendar.

title: How to Capitalize ERP or Order Management System Implementation Costs
description: Recording the cost of implementing a new OMS or ERP as an intangible asset under IAS 38.
explanation: ERP and OMS implementation costs meeting the IAS 38 capitalization criteria are intangible assets. They are amortized over the expected useful life (typically 5-7 years).

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Capitalizable ERP/OMS implementation costs include: software licenses, external consultant implementation fees (directly attributable configuration and development work), and internal staff costs directly attributable to the implementation project. NOT capitalizable: training costs, data migration testing (generally), general overheads allocated to the project, and post-implementation maintenance. Maintain a project cost ledger to segregate capitalizable from non-capitalizable costs.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: IAS 38 implementation capitalization is heavily scrutinized: (1) The system must be in the 'development phase' (not just research/evaluation) — costs incurred before management commits to the specific system are expensed, (2) Training costs are explicitly excluded under IAS 38, (3) The useful life assessment must be documented and defensible — 5 years is standard but shorter lives are appropriate for rapidly-evolving SaaS systems, (4) Impairment must be considered if the system is replaced or abandoned.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Project capitalization policy (phases, cost types included/excluded), implementation project cost ledger (by cost type and phase), IAS 38 phase analysis (research vs. development), vendor contract and invoices, useful life determination memo, and impairment assessment at first use and annually.

title: How to Record Monthly Amortization of a Capitalized ERP or Platform System
description: Recognizing monthly amortization expense on a capitalized ERP or OMS implementation over its useful life.
explanation: A JOD 35,000 ERP system amortized over 5 years generates JOD 583/month of amortization. This expense is a G&A technology cost.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set up an auto-journal entry at go-live date to generate monthly amortization automatically. Monitor the accumulated amortization balance against the gross intangible asset value — full amortization means the asset is fully depreciated and should be reviewed for continued use or derecognition. If the ERP is replaced before the end of its useful life, the remaining net book value must be written off as an impairment or disposal loss.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Amortization is tested for: (1) The amortization start date is the go-live date (when the asset is available for use), not the purchase or implementation start date, (2) The amortization method is straight-line (standard for ERP systems unless usage pattern suggests otherwise), (3) The remaining useful life is reassessed annually — a system that will be replaced in 2 years should have its remaining life shortened accordingly.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Fixed asset / intangible asset register entry (gross value, amortization start date, useful life, monthly charge), accumulated amortization schedule, annual useful life reassessment memo, and impairment review at each balance sheet date.

title: How to Record VAT Output Tax on Domestic E-commerce Sales in Jordan
description: Charging and recording 16% VAT on taxable product sales to Jordanian customers for ISTD remittance.
explanation: E-commerce stores registered for VAT in Jordan must charge 16% on taxable goods. Some product categories (basic foods, medicines) are exempt. The tax is collected on behalf of the ISTD.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure tax codes in the ERP by product category: standard-rated (16%), zero-rated (0%), and exempt. The tax code should automatically apply when a customer order is invoiced. VAT amounts should flow directly to the VAT Output Tax Payable account without manual intervention. Monthly, the VAT Output ledger is reconciled to the VAT return before submission to ISTD.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: ISTD may audit VAT compliance: (1) Is VAT charged on all standard-rated products — no categories incorrectly classified as exempt? (2) Does the VAT Output balance in the GL match the output tax reported on the VAT return? (3) Is the gross VAT inclusive price shown to customers and is the breakdown of pre-tax price + VAT on invoices? (4) Are free samples and barter transactions (like influencer seedings) assessed for output VAT?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Sales invoices showing VAT breakdown, VAT output tax register by period, product category tax classification schedule, monthly VAT return filed with ISTD, and reconciliation of VAT return to GL output tax account.

title: How to Record Recoverable VAT Input Tax on Inventory Purchases in Jordan
description: Separating 16% VAT paid to suppliers as a recoverable input tax asset, not part of inventory cost.
explanation: VAT paid on inventory is a recoverable input tax — not part of the inventory cost. It is offset against VAT collected on sales when filing the monthly return.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The ERP should automatically split the supplier invoice into the net inventory cost (to Merchandise Inventory) and the VAT component (to VAT Input Tax) based on the tax code on the purchase order. This is standard in any VAT-compliant ERP. Verify that the tax registration number on supplier invoices is valid — input tax claims on invoices from unregistered suppliers may be disallowed by ISTD.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: ISTD auditors check input tax claims for: (1) Valid VAT invoices from registered suppliers (supplier TRN must be on the invoice), (2) Input tax only claimed on business-purpose purchases — personal expenses disallowed, (3) Input tax on items with restricted deductibility (entertainment, passenger vehicles) is correctly limited or excluded, (4) The input tax amount in the GL matches the total input tax on purchase invoices.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Supplier VAT invoices (must show supplier TRN, net amount, VAT rate, VAT amount), purchase ledger by supplier, VAT input tax register, ISTD check of supplier registration status for high-value claims, and monthly VAT return reconciling input tax claimed to invoices.

title: How to Record VAT Paid on Imported Goods at Jordanian Customs
description: Capturing the recoverable import VAT paid at the border when bringing inventory into Jordan.
explanation: VAT paid at customs on imported goods is a separate input tax from the supplier invoice VAT. It is recorded as a recoverable asset and offset against VAT output on future sales.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Import VAT is paid at customs clearance, separately from the supplier invoice. Record it as a distinct VAT Input Tax asset (not part of inventory cost). When preparing the monthly VAT return, import VAT is included in total input tax available for offset against output VAT. The customs clearance declaration (Bill of Lading / Customs Form) is the supporting document.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Import VAT claims require the customs clearance declaration as supporting evidence: (1) The customs form must match the inventory received (same shipment reference), (2) Import VAT paid must be supported by the customs payment receipt, (3) Any import VAT on exempt or restricted-input items must be excluded from the recoverable claim.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Customs clearance declaration (Bayan Jumruki), import VAT payment receipt, cash payment confirmation, landed cost schedule showing import VAT separately from customs duty, and monthly VAT return showing import VAT input included.

title: How to Apply VAT Reverse Charge on Digital Advertising from Google, Meta, and TikTok
description: Self-assessing VAT on digital advertising invoices from foreign platforms when operating in Jordan.
explanation: E-commerce businesses buying digital advertising from foreign platforms must self-assess VAT in Jordan. The input and output entries typically net to zero but are required on the VAT return.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure reverse charge tax codes for foreign service providers (Google, Meta, TikTok, Amazon Web Services, Shopify). When a foreign invoice is posted, the ERP should automatically generate both the output VAT (liability) and input VAT (asset) entries. These net to zero on the cash flow but must appear correctly on both lines of the VAT return. Many Jordanian businesses fail to report reverse charge VAT — this is a compliance risk.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: ISTD increasingly audits reverse charge compliance for digital services: (1) Is reverse charge applied to all foreign digital service invoices (not just advertising — also SaaS subscriptions, cloud services, marketplace fees)? (2) Do the reverse charge amounts on the VAT return reconcile to the total foreign service invoices paid? (3) Has the business correctly identified which foreign services are subject to reverse charge vs. those that may be zero-rated under a tax treaty?
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Foreign supplier invoices (Google Ads, Meta, TikTok billing statements), reverse charge calculation per invoice (16% on net invoice amount), VAT return showing reverse charge output and input entries, and a schedule of all foreign service providers subject to reverse charge.

title: How to Record the Monthly VAT Remittance Payment to ISTD Jordan
description: Paying the net VAT liability (output minus input) to the Income and Sales Tax Department.
explanation: The net VAT payable = Output VAT collected - Input VAT recoverable. Only the difference is remitted to the ISTD. If input exceeds output, a refund claim is submitted.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Monthly VAT returns must be filed with ISTD by the 30th of the month following the tax period. The return is filed electronically via the ISTD portal. Before filing, reconcile: (1) VAT Output ledger to total taxable sales per OMS, (2) VAT Input ledger to total supplier invoices and customs declarations. The cash payment to ISTD closes out the net VAT payable for the period.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: ISTD conducts periodic VAT audits covering up to 5 years. Key risks: (1) Output VAT understated due to unregistered sales or incorrect tax codes, (2) Input VAT overclaimed due to invalid invoices or non-business expenses, (3) Late filing — penalties apply after the due date, (4) Reverse charge VAT on digital services not reported, (5) VAT on related-party transactions at non-arm's length prices.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Filed VAT return (ISTD portal confirmation), VAT output and input reconciliation to GL, bank transfer confirmation for VAT payment, and all supporting invoices for the period (retained for 5 years per ISTD requirements).

title: How to Capitalize Customs Duty into Imported Inventory Cost
description: Adding import duties paid at the Jordanian customs border to the cost of imported inventory under IAS 2.
explanation: Import duties are part of the landed cost of inventory and must be capitalized under IAS 2. They increase the inventory cost and therefore the COGS when items are eventually sold.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Customs duties are an element of the landed cost and must be allocated across inventory items in the shipment. Use the same allocation method as freight (by value, weight, or volume) — apply consistently. The per-unit duty cost increases the unit cost in the ERP, flowing through to COGS when items are sold. Customs duties are not recoverable as input VAT — do not post them to the VAT Input account.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: A common error is expensing customs duties rather than capitalizing them — this understates inventory and understates COGS in the period of sale. Auditors check: (1) Customs duties are included in the landed cost calculation, (2) Duty rates applied match the tariff classification for the product, (3) Any duty drawback or refund credits are applied as a reduction to inventory cost when received.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Customs clearance declaration (showing duty rate and amount per product), duty payment receipt, landed cost allocation schedule (showing duty allocated per SKU), and duty rate schedule or tariff classification documentation for key product categories.

title: How to Accrue Corporate Income Tax for an E-commerce Company in Jordan
description: Recording the annual income tax provision on the e-commerce company's taxable profit at year-end.
explanation: Income tax is accrued at year-end based on taxable profit. Taxable income may differ from accounting profit due to non-deductible expenses and timing differences.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The income tax provision requires a tax computation that adjusts accounting profit for: (1) Non-deductible expenses (entertainment, fines, provisions not yet deductible), (2) Tax allowances (accelerated capital allowances if applicable), (3) Exempt income. The resulting taxable income is multiplied by the applicable tax rate (20% for most Jordanian companies, with lower rates for small businesses). Quarterly prepayments to ISTD offset the final tax payable.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Income tax provisions are a high-priority audit area: (1) The tax computation reconciles accounting profit to taxable income with clear adjustments, (2) Deferred tax is assessed for material temporary differences (e.g., accelerated amortization of ERP), (3) Quarterly tax prepayments made during the year are properly credited against the final liability, (4) The effective tax rate is reasonable — significant deviation from the statutory rate requires explanation.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Annual tax computation (accounting profit to taxable profit bridge), income tax return filed with ISTD, quarterly tax prepayment receipts, deferred tax assessment, and any ISTD tax assessment notices or correspondence.

title: How to Withhold Tax on Fees Paid to Foreign Marketplaces Like Amazon and Noon
description: Applying Jordanian withholding tax when paying commissions or fees to foreign marketplace operators.
explanation: Payments to foreign entities for services (commissions, platform fees) may require withholding tax deduction. Jordan has tax treaties with several countries that reduce or eliminate this obligation.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure withholding tax codes for payments to foreign service providers in the ERP. The WHT rate depends on: (1) Whether Jordan has a double tax treaty with the recipient's country, (2) The nature of the service (royalties, technical services, management fees each have different treaty rates), (3) Whether the foreign entity provides a tax residency certificate to claim treaty relief. Without a treaty or certificate, Jordan's domestic WHT rate (10% for service payments) applies.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: WHT non-compliance is a common finding in ISTD audits of e-commerce businesses: (1) All material payments to foreign platforms (Amazon, Google, Meta, Shopify) should be assessed for WHT applicability, (2) WHT must be remitted to ISTD within 30 days of the payment, (3) WHT certificates must be issued to the foreign payee, (4) Treaty claims must be supported by valid tax residency certificates from the foreign entity.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Foreign supplier invoice, WHT calculation (payment amount × applicable rate), WHT withholding certificate issued to foreign payee, ISTD WHT remittance confirmation, double tax treaty reference (if rate reduced), and tax residency certificate from foreign entity (if treaty relief claimed).

title: How to Record an Inventory Financing Drawdown from a Trade Credit Line
description: Using a revolving trade finance facility to purchase inventory ahead of peak season, recorded as a liability.
explanation: Inventory financing allows e-commerce businesses to stock up for peak periods (Ramadan, Black Friday) without tying up cash. The facility is repaid as stock sells.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Trade finance drawdowns should be linked to specific purchase orders in the ERP so that when the inventory is received, the asset and the facility payable are created simultaneously. Track the facility utilization against the approved credit limit. As inventory sells and cash is received, repay the facility — some lenders require direct repayment from sales proceeds (collection sweeps). Interest on the facility should be expensed monthly, not capitalized into inventory unless the criteria for borrowing costs under IAS 23 are met.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Trade finance facilities are tested for: (1) Covenant compliance — sales-to-inventory ratios and other financial covenants from the facility agreement, (2) Is interest being expensed correctly and timely? (3) Are drawdowns linked to actual inventory receipts — a lender may require inventory confirmation, (4) The facility is classified as current if repayable within 12 months — reclassification errors affect working capital ratios.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Trade finance facility agreement (limit, drawdown conditions, interest rate, repayment terms), drawdown request and confirmation, purchase order and goods received note, monthly interest calculation, and facility utilization schedule.

title: How to Record a Supplier Early Payment Discount
description: Capturing the saving when a supplier offers a cash discount for settling the invoice ahead of the due date.
explanation: Early payment discounts reduce the effective cost of inventory. The saving is credited back to inventory (perpetual system) as the goods cost less than originally recorded.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In a perpetual inventory system, the early payment discount reduces the inventory cost of the items purchased. If those items have already been sold (COGS already recognized), the discount should be credited to Purchase Discounts income rather than inventory. Configure the ERP to check whether the discounted inventory has been sold before posting the discount to inventory vs. income.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Early payment discounts are relatively straightforward but auditors check: (1) Are discounts taken within the discount period? Discounts taken after the discount deadline may not be accepted by the supplier, (2) For significant discount amounts, is the net cost correctly flowing through to COGS when items are sold? (3) Discounts from related-party suppliers should be assessed at arm's-length pricing.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Supplier invoice showing discount terms (e.g., 2/10 net 30), early payment confirmation (invoice paid within discount period), bank transfer showing net payment, inventory cost adjustment entry, and supplier account reconciliation.

title: How to Record a Merchant Cash Advance Drawdown from a Fintech Lender
description: Accounting for a lump-sum advance against future sales revenue, with the factor fee treated as a finance cost.
