description: Processing a monthly mortgage installment, splitting between interest income and principal reduction.
explanation: Mortgage repayments are split between interest (recognized as income) and principal reduction (reduces the loan balance). In early years of a mortgage, most of the payment is interest. The split is determined by the amortization schedule generated at origination.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE CL module, the system automatically generates the split based on the loan's amortization schedule (principal + interest). The schedule adjusts if the customer makes early repayments. In SAP CML, the repayment schedule is fixed at origination and deviations trigger a schedule recalculation.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test that the interest component matches the system-calculated amount based on the outstanding principal balance and the EIR. Any manual override of the principal/interest split requires dual authorization. CBJ requires that prepayment penalties (if charged) are disclosed in the loan agreement.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Loan repayment schedule, monthly account statement, system repayment allocation report, and customer payment receipt.

title: Auto Loan Disbursement (Retail Vehicles)
description: Disbursing a 3-year auto loan directly to a car dealer on behalf of a retail customer.
explanation: Auto loans are typically disbursed directly to the dealer (not the customer). The vehicle registration certificate must show the bank's lien. EIR method applies to origination fees. Auto loans are usually for shorter terms (3-5 years) compared to home mortgages.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE CL, auto loans use a specific product type with collateral category 'vehicle'. The vehicle registration and lien details are captured in the collateral module. CBJ requires auto loans to be disbursed to the dealer, not credited to the customer's account.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that the vehicle registration in the Traffic Department shows the bank's lien (rahn) before or simultaneously with disbursement. Loans disbursed before the lien is registered are under-collateralized. Insurance policy assignment to the bank must also be in place.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Vehicle purchase invoice, Traffic Department registration showing bank lien, insurance policy assignment, credit approval, dealer payment confirmation, and customer loan agreement.

title: Personal Loan Installment Collected
description: Collecting a monthly installment on a personal (unsecured) loan via direct debit from salary account.
explanation: For salary-deducted loans, the bank debits the customer's salary account on the salary credit date. This provides natural collateral for unsecured personal loans. The installment is split between principal and interest per the amortization schedule.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE, direct debit mandates are configured so the CL (loan) module triggers an automatic debit on the customer's CASA account on the due date. CBJ regulations require that salary deductions for loan repayments do not exceed 50% of the net salary (debt burden ratio).
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test the debt burden ratio compliance — if the total monthly loan deductions exceed 50% of net salary, the loan should not have been approved. Rejected salary debits (insufficient funds) automatically move the loan to arrears status and trigger an early warning flag.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Direct debit mandate, salary certificate, debt burden ratio calculation at origination, monthly debit confirmation, and arrears report for any missed payments.

title: Credit Card Facility — Limit Approval (Off-Balance-Sheet)
description: Approving and recording an undrawn credit card limit as an off-balance-sheet commitment.
explanation: An approved but undrawn credit card limit is an off-balance-sheet contingent exposure. For ECL under IFRS 9, undrawn credit card limits require an ECL provision calculated on the 12-month expected drawdown multiplied by PD and LGD.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Credit card limits are managed in the Card Management System (CMS), not the core banking system. The off-balance-sheet exposure must be extracted from CMS and included in the IFRS 9 ECL model. CBJ capital adequacy rules apply a 20% credit conversion factor to undrawn revolving retail commitments.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check that undrawn credit card limits are included in the ECL model. A common omission is excluding card limits from the IFRS 9 provision calculation, which understates the provision. CBJ inspectors test whether the approved limits comply with the income/salary-based limits in the bank's credit policy.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Credit card application, credit approval, card issuance confirmation, credit limit system record, and inclusion in ECL model data extract.

title: Credit Card Purchase — Transaction Billed to Cardholder
description: Recording a cardholder's retail purchase on their credit card.
explanation: The issuing bank earns interchange income on each card transaction. The cardholder is billed the full amount; the merchant receives less (merchant discount rate minus interchange paid to the issuer). The net settlement to the merchant's bank reflects the full card scheme economics.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Card transactions are processed in the Card Management System. Settlement occurs through the card scheme (Visa/MC/JONET) T+1 or T+2. The CMS-to-GL interface posts the gross billing and net settlement. Interchange income is a key revenue line for retail banks and is tracked in the CMS before GL posting.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors reconcile CMS transaction volumes to the interchange income in the GL. Unauthorized credit card transactions (fraud) that are processed before being blocked are a risk — the bank may need to absorb the loss if the chargeback dispute is resolved in the cardholder's favor.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Card scheme settlement statement, CMS daily transaction report, interchange rate schedule, and merchant settlement confirmation.

title: Credit Card Payment Received from Cardholder
description: Cardholder makes a full payment of their monthly credit card statement balance.
explanation: Full payment clears the credit card balance. No interest is charged if payment is received within the grace period. The payment reduces both the outstanding balance and the bank's exposure.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In the CMS, card payments are matched to the outstanding statement balance and posted as CASA debits. Minimum payment tracking (for revolvers) is also handled in CMS. IFRS 9 requires that revolving (minimum payment) customers are assessed for elevated credit risk and potentially staged to Stage 2.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors monitor the percentage of cardholders making only minimum payments (revolvers) vs. full payers (transactors). A rising revolver ratio indicates increasing credit risk in the portfolio. CBJ requires disclosure of the credit card NPL rate in regulatory returns.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Card payment confirmation, statement balance at payment date, CASA debit advice, and CMS payment processing report.

title: Credit Card Over-Limit Fee Charged
description: Charging a fee when a cardholder exceeds their approved credit limit.
explanation: Over-limit fees are recognized when charged. They are included in the cardholder's outstanding balance and accrue interest if not paid within the grace period. CBJ consumer protection rules require these fees to be disclosed in the card agreement.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: CMS automatically detects and applies over-limit fees per the product definition. The fee is added to the outstanding balance immediately. Some CMS systems allow blocking transactions that would exceed the limit — the bank's policy determines whether over-limit spending is permitted.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that over-limit fees are disclosed in the credit card agreement and comply with CBJ fee caps. Repeated over-limit situations without corrective action (credit limit increase or mandatory reduction) suggest inadequate credit monitoring.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Card agreement with fee schedule, CMS over-limit event log, fee billing confirmation, and CBJ fee cap compliance report.

title: Credit Card Late Payment Fee Charged
description: Charging a late fee when minimum payment is not received by the due date.

entries.account: Credit Card Late Payment Fee Income

explanation: Late fees are a significant revenue source for credit card portfolios. Under IFRS 15, they are recognized when charged (point-in-time performance obligation satisfied). They are added to the outstanding balance and trigger a credit risk flag in the monitoring system.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: CMS automatically charges the late fee on the day after the payment due date if minimum payment has not been received. The fee is capitalized into the outstanding balance. IFRS 9 staging rules: a single missed payment triggers early warning monitoring; 30 DPD triggers Stage 2 assessment.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors review the late fee income trend for unusual patterns. A spike in late fees may indicate portfolio stress. CBJ requires credit card delinquency (30+, 60+, 90+ DPD) to be reported. Late fees on Stage 3 accounts are recognized on a cash basis only.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: CMS payment due date and receipt date log, late fee billing report, delinquency report by DPD bucket, and reconciliation of late fee income to CMS.

title: Credit Card Cashback Reward Accrual
description: Accruing cashback rewards earned by cardholders on eligible purchases.
explanation: Cashback rewards are a cost of the card program. Under IFRS 15, they represent a reduction in transaction price (variable consideration) or a loyalty point liability. The bank accrues the expected cashback based on eligible spend patterns.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Cashback calculations are handled in the CMS's loyalty/rewards module. Monthly accruals are posted to the GL via the CMS-GL interface. Cashback is typically credited to the cardholder's statement balance quarterly or annually. The accrual rate must match the card product's cashback percentage.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test the accrual rate against the card product agreement. Underaccrual understates the liability and overstates profit. Unclaimed cashback that expires must be assessed for breakage revenue recognition under IFRS 15.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Cashback program terms, eligible spend volume report, cashback accrual calculation, CMS loyalty module report, and reconciliation of cashback liability to program data.

title: Consumer Loan Prepayment Penalty Income
description: Charging a prepayment penalty when a customer fully repays a personal loan before maturity.
explanation: On prepayment, the remaining loan balance and any unamortized origination fee are cleared. The prepayment penalty is point-in-time fee income. The deferred origination fee is accelerated to zero since the loan no longer exists.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE CL, early settlement closes the contract, automatically accelerates unamortized fees to P&L, and calculates the prepayment penalty per the penalty schedule in the product definition. In SAP CML, a 'termination' transaction triggers the same sequence.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: CBJ consumer protection regulations cap prepayment penalties for personal loans (typically 1-2% of outstanding balance). Penalties above the CBJ cap are illegal and subject to regulatory action. Auditors verify that penalties are disclosed in the original loan agreement.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Customer early settlement request, prepayment penalty calculation, revised loan statement showing zero balance, and CBJ cap compliance check.

title: Loan Restructuring — IFRS 9 Modification Assessment
description: Restructuring a distressed corporate loan — extending tenor and reducing interest rate — and assessing whether it is a substantial modification.
explanation: Under IFRS 9, if a modification is 'substantial' (present value of new cash flows differs by 10%+ from old cash flows discounted at the original EIR), the old loan is derecognized and a new loan is recognized. The difference is a modification gain or loss. If not substantial, a modification gain/loss is recognized but the original loan continues.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: IFRS 9 modification assessment requires a manual calculation comparing the present value of the revised cash flows (at original EIR) against the carrying amount. Most core banking systems do not automate this test — it is typically done in Excel and the result drives the accounting treatment. New EIR is calculated on the modified loan if derecognition occurs.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: This is a highly scrutinized area. Auditors test the 10% PV test calculation independently. Misclassification of a substantial modification as a non-substantial modification understates losses. Banks sometimes restructure loans to avoid NPL classification — 'evergreening' — which CBJ prohibits.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Restructuring agreement, original loan agreement, IFRS 9 modification assessment calculation workbook, credit committee approval, and CBJ notification if the restructuring affects NPL classification.

title: Term Loan Scheduled Principal Repayment
description: Receiving a scheduled quarterly principal repayment on a corporate term loan.
explanation: Scheduled principal repayments reduce the loan balance. They do not affect P&L (no income or expense). Interest income is recognized separately via the accrual entry. The outstanding balance post-repayment must update the ECL calculation.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE CL, scheduled repayments are automatically debited from the borrower's account on the due date (if direct debit mandate exists) or posted when funds are received. In SAP CML, the repayment schedule drives the expected cash flow; receipt posting is manual or via SWIFT/payment interface.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors reconcile loan repayment receipts to the repayment schedule. Missed scheduled repayments on their due date must be reflected immediately in the DPD counter and arrears report. Any waiver of a scheduled payment (holiday) requires credit committee approval.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Loan repayment schedule, debit confirmation from borrower account, updated loan statement, arrears report (showing zero DPD), and SWIFT payment confirmation (for large corporate repayments).

title: Term Loan Bullet Repayment at Maturity
description: Full repayment of a bullet (interest-only) term loan at its final maturity date.
explanation: Bullet loans repay the entire principal at maturity. This creates refinancing/concentration risk. Under IFRS 9, the bank must assess whether Stage 2/3 migration is needed in the period leading up to maturity if there are signs the borrower may not be able to refinance.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Bullet maturity events are tracked in the loan management system's maturity report. A reminder workflow should trigger 90-180 days before maturity to assess refinancing risk. In Oracle FLEXCUBE, the 'LIQD' event handles bullet loan liquidation. Any remaining accrued interest must be collected simultaneously.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check that bullet loans approaching maturity are in the credit monitoring watch list if refinancing risk is elevated. Loans that were repeatedly rolled at maturity without formal renewal are classified as evergreening — a CBJ prohibited practice.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Maturity notice to borrower, receipt confirmation, loan contract closure, reconciliation of all fees and accrued interest to zero, and credit monitoring sign-off.

title: Project Finance — Construction Phase Drawdown
description: Processing a drawdown on a project finance facility for infrastructure construction.
explanation: Project finance drawdowns are conditional on verified construction progress (typically confirmed by the lender's independent engineer). Funds often flow through a project escrow account to ensure proper application. The loan is non-recourse to the sponsor's balance sheet.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Project finance loans are managed in SAP CML with multiple tranches linked to construction milestones. In Oracle FLEXCUBE, each drawdown is a separate disbursement event. The Independent Engineer's report is a condition precedent for each drawdown — this CP must be cleared in the system before disbursement is allowed.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that Independent Engineer certification was received before each drawdown. Construction cost overruns not covered by contingency reserves affect the bank's security. CBJ project finance guidelines require quarterly monitoring reports from the bank.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Independent Engineer certification, construction progress report, drawdown certificate from borrower, CP clearance checklist, escrow account statement, and quarterly monitoring report.

title: Working Capital Facility Annual Renewal Fee
description: Charging a renewal fee when a corporate working capital (overdraft/revolving) facility is renewed for another year.
explanation: Annual facility renewal fees are deferred and recognized over the 12-month facility period. The bank's performance obligation is maintaining the credit facility available for drawdown. Upfront recognition of annual fees is incorrect under IFRS 15.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE CL, facility fees are charged via the 'PRLQ' (product liquidation) event at renewal. Deferral is typically managed outside the core banking system in a fee tracking spreadsheet or a dedicated fee management module. Monthly amortization credits fee income.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test fee revenue recognition policy — annual facility fees must be deferred, not taken upfront. A bank booking the full renewal fee in month 1 overstates income by 11/12 of the fee. This is a common finding in institutions transitioning to IFRS 15.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Facility renewal letter, fee billing advice, deferred fee schedule, and reconciliation of deferred fee balance to active facility register.

title: Invoice Discounting / Supply Chain Finance
description: Advancing funds to a supplier by purchasing their receivable from the corporate anchor buyer at a discount.
explanation: The bank buys the invoice at a discount (JOD 98,000 for a JOD 100,000 invoice). The JOD 2,000 discount is interest income earned over the invoice tenor. When the anchor buyer pays the full JOD 100,000 on due date, the income is fully recognized.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: SCF programs are typically managed on dedicated SCF platforms (Kyriba, FIS, proprietary) that interface with both the anchor buyer's ERP and the bank's core banking. In Oracle FLEXCUBE, SCF may be managed in the BC (Bills and Collections) module as discounted receivables. The anchor buyer's credit quality, not the supplier's, drives the ECL assessment.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors assess whether the SCF receivable is truly derecognized from the supplier's balance sheet or whether the bank is acting as principal. If the anchor buyer is also a major depositor/borrower, the SCF program may create related-party disclosure requirements. CBJ may classify some SCF structures as factoring (regulated).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: SCF master agreement with anchor buyer, individual invoice purchase confirmation, supplier invoice and delivery evidence, discount calculation, and anchor buyer notification of assignment.

title: Loan Watch-Listed — Stage 2 SICR Trigger
description: Moving a loan to Stage 2 based on qualitative deterioration signals before 30 DPD is reached.
explanation: IFRS 9 requires both quantitative and qualitative SICR assessment. A loan may move to Stage 2 even with zero DPD if: the borrower's revenue has declined significantly, a key contract was lost, or the sector is under stress. This forward-looking approach is a major change from IAS 39.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Qualitative SICR triggers require human judgment and are typically entered as manual overrides in SAP Credit Risk Analyzer or Oracle OBCL after RM escalation and credit review sign-off. The system generates the ECL uplift amount based on the updated stage and lifetime PD/LGD model.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors specifically test whether qualitative SICR criteria are applied consistently and not used to avoid Stage 2 (by setting criteria too loose). CBJ inspectors review watch list management practices and compare the bank's Stage 2 portfolio against industry peers.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Credit monitoring committee memo documenting SICR evidence, RM escalation note, updated credit assessment, ALCO/Risk Committee approval for Stage 2 classification, and ECL calculation before and after.

title: Debt-Equity Swap — NPL Converted to Equity Stake
description: Converting a non-performing corporate loan into equity shares in the borrower company.

entries.account: Equity Investment in Borrower (at Fair Value)

explanation: The equity received is measured at fair value. The loan and its ECL provision are derecognized. The difference between the net carrying amount of the loan (JOD 800,000 after JOD 700,000 provision) and the fair value of equity received is the gain or loss. If equity fair value equals net carrying amount, no gain/loss arises.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Debt-equity swaps require CBJ prior approval (banks are generally restricted in equity holdings). The transaction requires both the core banking system (loan derecognition) and the investments system (equity recording). A fair value determination by an independent valuer is mandatory.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: External auditors require an independent fair value assessment of the equity received. CBJ limits banks' equity holdings in non-financial companies to a percentage of capital. The equity investment is subsequently measured at FVTPL or equity method depending on ownership percentage and influence.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: CBJ prior approval, EGM resolution from borrower company authorizing the swap, independent valuation of equity received, restructuring agreement, and shareholder register update showing the bank's new equity stake.

title: Collateral Foreclosure — Property Taken in Lieu of Debt
description: Taking ownership of pledged property after foreclosure proceedings against an NPL borrower.
explanation: OREO is initially recorded at the lower of the loan's net carrying amount (after ECL) or the property's fair value less costs to sell. The loan is derecognized. Any shortfall between the OREO value and the net loan is an additional loss. Holding OREO is a regulatory concern for banks.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: OREO is classified as a non-financial asset and is tracked in a separate register outside the core banking loan system. In SAP FI, OREO is managed as a fixed asset (FA module) with regular impairment testing. CBJ sets limits on the period a bank can hold OREO (typically 2-3 years before forced disposal).
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors perform OREO impairment testing at each reporting date using current property valuations. OREO that has declined in value after foreclosure requires additional impairment charges. CBJ requires detailed OREO schedules in regulatory reports, and properties held beyond the permitted period attract regulatory penalties.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Court foreclosure order, Land Registration transfer to bank's name, independent property valuation, OREO register entry, initial impairment assessment, and CBJ notification of OREO acquisition.

title: OREO — Depreciation / Impairment Charge
description: Recording impairment or depreciation on real estate owned by the bank following foreclosure.
explanation: OREO is not depreciated in the traditional sense (it's held for sale, not for use). Instead, it is tested for impairment against current market value (less costs to sell). Declines in property value since foreclosure create impairment charges in the income statement.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: OREO impairment is assessed semi-annually (or annually) using updated property valuations. The calculation compares current fair value less costs to sell against the carrying amount. SAP AM (Asset Management) module can be used to track OREO if the bank sets up OREO as an asset class.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors request current independent valuations for all OREO properties. Properties without an updated valuation (over 12 months old) are marked as findings. OREO held for more than CBJ's permitted period without disposal requires explanation and may attract regulatory provisions.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Current independent property valuation, impairment calculation worksheet, OREO register with acquisition cost and current carrying amount, and Board approval for impairment charges above a threshold.

title: OREO Sold — Gain on Disposal
description: Selling a foreclosed property at a price above its carrying amount.
explanation: On sale, the OREO and its accumulated impairment are derecognized. The gain equals the proceeds minus the net carrying amount. OREO sale gains are presented as Other Income. Sales proceeds are often used to partially repay other related NPLs.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In SAP AM, OREO disposal is processed via a retirement transaction that calculates the gain/loss automatically based on carrying amount vs. sale price. In Oracle FLEXCUBE, OREO disposal is a manual GL entry supported by the property sale documentation. Capital gains tax implications must be assessed.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the sale price is arm's length (not sold at undervalue to connected parties). The Land Registration transfer to the buyer must be completed for revenue recognition. Related-party sales of OREO require disclosure and CBJ notification.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Property sale agreement, Land Registration transfer confirmation, sale proceeds receipt, capital gains tax assessment, gain/loss calculation, and CBJ notification (for significant disposals).

title: NPL Debt Restructure — Principal Haircut (Forgiveness)
description: Agreeing to forgive a portion of principal as part of a formal debt restructuring for an NPL corporate borrower.
explanation: A principal haircut (debt forgiveness) is recognized as a write-off of the forgiven amount. If fully provisioned, no P&L impact at the time of haircut. The remaining loan balance is restructured with new terms. A SICR reversal assessment is performed after the restructuring.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Principal haircuts require Board/BCC approval and CBJ notification. In Oracle FLEXCUBE, the outstanding principal is manually reduced and the ECL provision is correspondingly released. The loan contract is modified to reflect new terms. A new EIR is calculated on the restructured balance.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the haircut is economically justified and not used to clean up the balance sheet without genuine credit improvement. The restructured loan enters a 'probation period' — CBJ guidance typically requires 12+ months of clean payment before Stage 2 reduction. Tax implications of debt forgiveness must be assessed.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Board/BCC approval for haircut, restructuring agreement with new terms, CBJ notification, tax opinion on debt forgiveness income to borrower, updated credit assessment, and new repayment schedule.

title: Murabaha — Bank Purchases Asset (Islamic Finance)
description: Bank purchases a commodity or asset from a supplier to sell it to the customer at a markup under a Murabaha contract.
explanation: In a Murabaha, the bank must genuinely purchase and own the asset before selling it to the customer. This purchase step creates a transitory asset on the bank's balance sheet. The asset must not be sold to the customer before the bank has taken ownership (no back-to-back same-day transactions without genuine ownership).

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Islamic banking modules in Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic (or dedicated systems like Path Solutions iMAL) handle Murabaha specifically. The asset purchase and sale are separate transactions in the system. Some CBJ-regulated Islamic banks use a commodity Murabaha structure on LME commodities to achieve a cash financing equivalent while maintaining Shariah compliance.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Shariah Board compliance review is mandatory. The bank's Shariah supervisory board must confirm that the asset purchase is genuine and that ownership risk (even if brief) is borne by the bank before the sale. Auditors verify that the profit rate is disclosed upfront (not variable) and matches the Murabaha agreement.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Supplier invoice and delivery confirmation, Murabaha agreement, Shariah Board approval/fatwa, customer's purchase offer, profit rate disclosure, and CBJ Islamic finance reporting schedule.

title: Murabaha — Asset Sold to Customer at Cost-Plus Markup
description: Bank sells the purchased asset to the customer at cost plus an agreed profit margin under the Murabaha contract.
explanation: The Murabaha profit (JOD 20,000 markup on JOD 100,000 cost) is deferred and recognized over the repayment period. The full receivable (JOD 120,000) is recorded. The deferred profit is released monthly as the customer makes installments.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic, the Murabaha contract records the cost price, profit amount, and tenor. The deferred profit is automatically amortized over the installment schedule. The accounting treatment mirrors a conventional loan in economic substance but differs in form — the profit is not 'interest'.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify deferred profit amortization matches the Murabaha installment schedule. Early settlement of Murabaha (where the bank returns part of the unearned profit) must be reflected correctly. The profit rate must be fixed at inception — any variable or restructured profit calculation requires fresh Shariah approval.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Murabaha sale agreement, installment schedule, deferred profit amortization schedule, early settlement policy, and Shariah Board sign-off on the contract structure.

title: Murabaha Installment Collected
description: Collecting a monthly Murabaha installment from the customer.
explanation: Each installment reduces the Murabaha receivable principal and releases a portion of the deferred profit to income. The income recognition mirrors the EIR method on a conventional loan, though Shariah-compliant structuring requires the profit to be fixed.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic, installment collection is automated. The system splits each payment into principal reduction and profit release per the amortization schedule. Late payment fees in Islamic banking must be structured as 'donation' to charity (not bank income) to avoid riba — this is a key Shariah compliance requirement.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors confirm the profit recognition pattern matches the amortization schedule. Late payment fees collected and retained by the bank (rather than donated to charity) are a Shariah compliance violation and audit finding. NPL Murabaha receivables must have profit recognition suspended.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Installment collection confirmation, amortization schedule, deferred profit release schedule, and quarterly Shariah compliance report.

title: Ijara — Bank Purchases Asset to Lease to Customer
description: Bank purchases equipment to lease to a customer under an Ijara (Islamic leasing) contract.
explanation: In an Ijara, the bank is the lessor and must own the asset. Unlike Murabaha, the bank retains asset ownership throughout the lease term. The bank bears ownership risks (e.g., major damage not caused by the lessee). The asset is depreciated by the bank, not the lessee.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Ijara assets are tracked in the bank's fixed asset module (SAP AM or Oracle FA) separate from OREO and operating assets. In Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic, Ijara contracts link the lease schedule to the asset record. From the lessee's perspective, IFRS 16 applies — they record a right-of-use asset and lease liability.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Shariah Board must confirm the Ijara structure is compliant — the bank must bear ownership risk (takaful/insurance for major damage). Auditors check the depreciation rate applied to Ijara assets reflects their economic life. CBJ may classify Ijara receivables as loans for regulatory capital purposes.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Asset purchase invoice, Shariah Board approval, Ijara contract, asset insurance policy (with bank as policyholder), depreciation schedule, and CBJ regulatory treatment confirmation.

title: Ijara Monthly Rental Income Collected
description: Collecting monthly rental payment from a lessee under an Ijara contract.
explanation: Rental income from Ijara contracts is recognized as earned over the lease period. It represents the return on the bank's ownership of the leased asset. Unlike conventional loan interest, rental is for the use of the asset — Shariah compliant as long as the bank retains ownership risk.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic, Ijara rental billing is automated per the rental schedule in the contract. In SAP, a leasing management module (if available) handles the rental schedule. Rental income is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term unless another basis better represents the usage pattern.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check that rental rates are market-appropriate. Variable rental Ijara (where rental is linked to a benchmark like JOIBOR) must be approved by the Shariah Board as a permissible reference rate. Overdue rentals must be suspended if the lessee is in default (similar to NPL interest suspension).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Ijara contract with rental schedule, payment receipt, rental billing advice, and delinquency tracking for overdue rentals.

title: Ijara Asset — Monthly Depreciation
description: Depreciating a bank-owned Ijara asset over its economic life.
explanation: Ijara assets are depreciated by the bank (lessor) over the asset's useful life — not just the lease term. The rental income must exceed the depreciation charge for the Ijara to be economically profitable. The net spread is the bank's profit margin.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Depreciation is automated in the fixed asset module (SAP AM, Oracle FA). The depreciation method (straight-line is most common for banking Ijara assets) and rate must be documented and approved by the bank's asset policy. Residual value assumptions affect the depreciation charge.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check that the total rental income over the Ijara term exceeds the acquisition cost (confirming the asset generates economic benefits). If the Ijara asset is expected to be transferred to the lessee at the end of the term (Ijara Muntahia Bitamleek), IFRS 16 recognition for the lessee is triggered.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Asset capitalization record, depreciation rate and method documentation, useful life assessment, and reconciliation of accumulated depreciation to the asset register.

title: Ijara Muntahia — Asset Title Transferred to Lessee at End of Lease
description: Transferring ownership of the leased asset to the lessee at a nominal price at lease end.
explanation: In an Ijara Muntahia Bitamleek, the ownership transfer at lease end is the intended conclusion. The asset is fully or nearly fully depreciated. The gain/loss on disposal is the difference between the book value and the nominal transfer price. This is a Shariah-compliant alternative to a hire-purchase.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The title transfer is documented via a separate Hiba (gift) agreement or a sale agreement at nominal price, distinct from the Ijara contract. In SAP AM, the asset is retired with proceeds equal to the nominal price. The Shariah Board typically requires these to be separate legal documents executed at the end of the lease.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the transfer of ownership is formalized via Land Registration (for property) or Transport Ministry records (for vehicles). The two contracts (Ijara and Hiba/sale) must be genuinely separate to satisfy Shariah compliance. Combined contracts are not Shariah-compliant.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Lease end confirmation, Hiba or nominal sale agreement, asset transfer registration confirmation (Land Department or Traffic), Shariah Board sign-off on the transfer structure, and final account reconciliation.

title: Musharaka — Bank's Capital Contribution
description: Bank contributes capital to a joint venture business under a Musharaka (partnership) structure.
explanation: Musharaka is an equity-participation Islamic finance structure. The bank becomes a partner in the business, sharing profits and losses according to an agreed ratio. This is classified as an equity investment — not a loan. It bears different capital treatment under CBJ Basel III.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Musharaka investments are recorded in the bank's investment ledger, not the loan ledger. In Islamic banking systems (Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic, iMAL), there is a dedicated Musharaka module. CBJ capital adequacy rules may assign a 100% or 250% risk weight to Musharaka investments, significantly impacting RWA.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Shariah Board approval is required. The profit-sharing ratio must be specified and agreed upfront. Auditors verify that the bank monitors the Musharaka venture's financial performance and that its share of profits/losses is correctly accrued. Loss absorption beyond the capital contribution is not required (limited partnership structure).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Musharaka agreement with profit/loss sharing ratios, Shariah Board approval, capital contribution receipt, CBJ equity investment limit compliance, and quarterly venture financial statements.

title: Musharaka Profit Distribution Received
description: Receiving the bank's share of profit from a Musharaka venture.
explanation: Musharaka profit distributions are recognized when the venture declares its profit and the bank's share is determinable. This income is Shariah-compliant profit-sharing, not interest. It appears in the income statement under 'Income from Islamic Finance Products'.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Profit distributions from Musharaka ventures are manually processed based on the venture's financial statements. In Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic, the income recognition journal is posted by the Islamic Finance Operations team upon receipt of the venture's profit confirmation.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that profit distributions are supported by the venture's audited or management accounts. Distributions exceeding reported profits are a finding. If the venture makes a loss, the bank must recognize its proportionate share as an expense.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Musharaka venture financial statements (audited preferred), profit distribution certificate, profit-sharing ratio calculation, and Shariah Board confirmation that the profit distribution is compliant.

title: Sukuk Investment Purchased
description: Bank purchases government or corporate Sukuk (Islamic bonds) for its investment portfolio.
explanation: Sukuk are Shariah-compliant securities representing ownership in an underlying asset or pool of assets. IFRS 9 classification (FVOCI or amortized cost) depends on the business model and whether cash flows pass the SPPI test. CBJ government Sukuk are typically HQLA-eligible.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Sukuk are managed in the bank's securities investment system (Oracle FLEXCUBE SM or SAP Bank Analyzer). For government Sukuk, the CBJ/CSD (Jordan Securities Depository) is the custodian. SPPI test must be documented at purchase for IFRS 9 classification. Unlike bonds, Sukuk represent ownership, not debt — the SPPI analysis may be more complex.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors perform the SPPI test documentation review for each Sukuk. Sukuk with complex underlying structures (equity-based) may fail the SPPI test and require FVTPL classification. CBJ Sukuk used in repo transactions (as collateral) must be tracked as encumbered in the HQLA buffer.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Sukuk prospectus/issuance documents, SPPI test documentation, business model assessment, purchase settlement confirmation (CSD), Bloomberg pricing at purchase, and custodian holding confirmation.

title: Sukuk Periodic Profit Payment Received
description: Receiving a semi-annual profit payment (equivalent to a coupon) on a held Sukuk investment.
explanation: Sukuk periodic profit payments are the Shariah-compliant equivalent of bond coupon payments. The accrued profit receivable (recognized monthly via EIR) is cleared when cash is received. The income line is labeled 'Sukuk Profit Income' rather than 'Interest Income'.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic SM module, Sukuk profit accrual is automated using the agreed profit rate. Payment notification comes from the Sukuk issuer's trustee and is matched to the accrued receivable in the system. WHT (if applicable) is deducted by the issuer before payment.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors reconcile received profit payments to the accrued receivable. Late profit payments from distressed Sukuk issuers trigger IFRS 9 staging assessment. For Ijara Sukuk, auditors verify the underlying asset generating the rental income exists and is properly maintained.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Sukuk trustee payment advice, accrued profit reconciliation, WHT deduction confirmation (if any), and updated Sukuk holding schedule.

title: Diminishing Musharaka — Customer Purchases a Unit from Bank
description: In a Diminishing Musharaka (home finance), the customer buys one unit of ownership from the bank, reducing the bank's share.
explanation: In Diminishing Musharaka, the bank and customer co-own a property. Over time, the customer buys the bank's share unit by unit. As units are purchased, the bank's ownership decreases. Rental income also decreases proportionally. This is the Islamic equivalent of a reducing-balance mortgage.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Diminishing Musharaka is one of the most complex products in Islamic banking systems. Oracle FLEXCUBE Islamic and iMAL have dedicated Diminishing Musharaka modules that track the ownership ratio, rental based on bank's share, and unit purchase payments separately. JMRC financing may be structured as Diminishing Musharaka for Islamic banks.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Shariah Board must approve the Diminishing Musharaka structure. Auditors verify that the rental charged each period is calculated on the bank's actual remaining ownership share (declining rental). Charging a fixed rental throughout the term when the bank's share is declining is a Shariah compliance issue.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Diminishing Musharaka agreement, unit purchase schedule, property co-ownership registration, rental calculation worksheet updated for each period, and Shariah Board approval.

title: Export LC — Advising Fee Income
description: Earning an advising fee for notifying the beneficiary (exporter) that a foreign bank has issued an LC in their favor.
explanation: Advising an LC means notifying the beneficiary of its existence. The advising bank has no payment obligation — it only verifies the LC's apparent authenticity. The fee is earned at the point of advising (IFRS 15 point-in-time performance obligation).

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE BC, the advising bank role is configured as a separate entity from the issuing bank. In SAP TRM-TF, the incoming LC (MT700) triggers the advising workflow and fee charging. SWIFT MT710 is used to re-advise an LC through another bank.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify advising fees are charged only when the LC is actually advised (SWIFT MT710 or direct advice to beneficiary). UCP 600 Article 9 governs the advising bank's obligations. If the advising bank adds its confirmation, a higher confirmation fee is charged separately.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Incoming SWIFT MT700, outgoing advice to exporter, fee billing confirmation, and SWIFT message log.

title: Export LC — Negotiation (Purchase of Documents)
description: Bank negotiates an export LC by purchasing compliant documents from the exporter and advancing funds before the issuing bank pays.
explanation: When a bank negotiates an LC, it advances funds to the exporter against compliant documents before the issuing bank pays. The negotiating bank bears the risk that the issuing bank may refuse the documents (discrepancies). Commission and interest are charged for this service.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE BC, negotiation creates an advance receivable against the issuing bank (or confirmed bank). SWIFT MT754 is sent to the issuing bank claiming reimbursement. The advance is liquidated when MT910 (credit advice) is received from the reimbursing bank.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check the country risk and bank risk of the issuing bank — negotiating LCs from low-rated banks in high-risk jurisdictions requires specific risk provisioning. The 5-day document examination period under UCP 600 must be observed before acceptance or rejection of documents.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Export LC documents (Bill of Lading, commercial invoice, etc.), document examination checklist, SWIFT MT754 (reimbursement claim), advance booking confirmation, and receipt of MT910 on settlement.

title: Standby Letter of Credit Issued
description: Issuing a standby LC that functions as a guarantee — payable only if the applicant fails to perform.
explanation: A Standby LC (SBLC) functions economically as a guarantee but is subject to UCP 600 or ISP98 rules for LCs. It carries the same capital adequacy treatment as a guarantee (50-100% CCF). Like regular LCs, it is off-balance-sheet until called.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In SAP TRM-TF and Oracle FLEXCUBE BC, SBLCs are managed as a sub-type of LC with a 'standby' flag. They require the same credit approval process as guarantees. The distinction from a commercial LC is important: SBLCs are typically governed by ISP98 while commercial LCs follow UCP 600.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors confirm the SBLC is captured in both off-balance-sheet disclosures and CBJ capital adequacy calculations. Called SBLCs (payment demands from beneficiaries) must be classified as on-balance-sheet liabilities immediately and the credit risk management team must be notified.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: SBLC application, credit approval, SBLC instrument issued to beneficiary, credit limit adjustment, and capital adequacy impact worksheet.

title: Bill of Exchange — Bank Acceptance
description: Bank accepts a bill of exchange drawn on it, creating a contingent payment obligation.
explanation: A bank acceptance is the bank's unconditional promise to pay the bill at maturity. It is a contingent liability until maturity when it becomes an on-balance-sheet payment obligation. Bankers acceptances are negotiable and may be sold in the secondary market.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Bankers acceptances are managed in SAP TRM-TF or Oracle FLEXCUBE BC as a trade finance instrument. Commission is charged to the customer for the bank's credit enhancement. At maturity, the bank pays the holder of the acceptance and debits the customer's account (or the customer defaults — triggering a loan advance).
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify all outstanding acceptances are captured in the off-balance-sheet schedule. Acceptances approaching maturity where the customer does not have funds to cover should be identified early and provisioned. CBJ capital adequacy rules assign a 100% CCF to bankers acceptances.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Original bill of exchange, bank's acceptance stamp and authorized signature, credit limit confirmation, commission billing, and register of outstanding acceptances by maturity date.

title: CBJ Bills Purchased (Open Market Operations)
description: Bank purchases CBJ Treasury Bills / Certificates of Deposit in the primary market.
explanation: CBJ bills are purchased at a discount to face value. They are the safest short-term investment for banks, qualifying as Level 1 HQLA. The discount accretes to par over the instrument's life using the EIR method, generating interest income.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: CBJ bill purchases are settled via RTGS directly to the CBJ. In SAP Bank Analyzer or Oracle FLEXCUBE SM, CBJ bills are set up as HTM or FVOCI instruments. Accretion of discount is automated in the interest accrual engine. CBJ bills are the primary instrument used in Jordan's interbank liquidity management.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify CBJ bills are correctly classified as Level 1 HQLA in the LCR calculation. Bills used as repo collateral are marked as encumbered and excluded from the unencumbered HQLA buffer. The discount accretion must use the EIR method per IFRS 9.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: CBJ auction allotment letter, purchase confirmation (RTGS settlement), discount accretion schedule, HQLA classification confirmation, and CSD holding statement.

title: Government Bond Coupon Received
description: Receiving a semi-annual coupon payment on a Jordanian government bond held in the investment portfolio.
explanation: The coupon is collected and clears the previously accrued interest receivable. No new P&L impact at the time of cash receipt — income was already accrued monthly via EIR. The net entry is simply a reclassification from accrued receivable to cash.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Coupon receipts on government bonds are credited to the bank's account at the CBJ (government bonds are typically held at CBJ as custodian). The core banking system matches the receipt to the accrued coupon receivable automatically in the securities management module.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors reconcile accrued interest receivable on government bonds to the coupon schedule. Unmatched coupons (received but not matched to an accrued receivable) indicate an accrual error. The CBJ holding statement serves as the independent confirmation of the bond position and coupon receipt.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: CBJ coupon payment notification, CSD/CBJ holding statement, accrued interest reconciliation, and investment income schedule.

title: Interest Rate Swap — Fair Value at Month-End
description: Marking to market a pay-fixed, receive-floating interest rate swap used to hedge a fixed-rate loan portfolio.

entries.account: Fair Value Gain on IRS (P&L or OCI)

explanation: Interest rate swaps are derivatives measured at FVTPL unless designated as hedging instruments. For a pay-fixed/receive-floating swap, rising interest rates increase the fair value (asset position). If the swap is designated as a fair value hedge, the hedged item's fair value change also goes to P&L.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: IRS fair values are calculated using the zero-coupon discount rate curve (typically sourced from Bloomberg/Reuters). In SAP TRM, IRS are managed as derivatives with daily MTM. In Oracle FLEXCUBE DV module, fair value calculations must be configured to use approved curve data. Hedge accounting documentation must be in place before trade date for OCI treatment.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test fair value model assumptions (discount rate curves, credit valuation adjustments). Hedge effectiveness must be tested prospectively (at designation) and retrospectively (at each reporting date). IRS with maturities beyond 10 years may require Level 2 or Level 3 fair value disclosure.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: ISDA Master Agreement, IRS term sheet, Bloomberg/Reuters rate curve at valuation date, hedge designation documentation (if applicable), MTM calculation workbook, and P&L/OCI allocation analysis.

title: Cross-Currency Swap — Fair Value at Month-End
description: Marking to market a cross-currency swap used to convert USD bond funding into JOD.

entries.account: Fair Value Gain on CCS (P&L or OCI)

explanation: A cross-currency swap exchanges principal and interest payments in two different currencies. Banks use them to hedge the FX risk of foreign currency funding. Fair value changes are driven by both interest rate differentials and spot FX rate movements.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Cross-currency swaps are among the most complex derivatives in terms of fair valuation — they require both an FX curve and an interest rate curve in each currency. SAP TRM and Oracle FLEXCUBE DV handle them, but Bloomberg SWPM or similar external tools are often used for independent pricing verification.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors and valuation specialists test the FX basis spread used in the CCS valuation. Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) and Debit Valuation Adjustment (DVA) must be included in the fair value for IFRS 13 compliance. Auditors also confirm the ISDA CSA (Credit Support Annex) collateral postings match the fair value positions.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: ISDA Master Agreement and CSA, CCS term sheet (SWIFT MT300), Bloomberg/Reuters valuation at reporting date, CVA/DVA calculation, and hedge designation documentation (if applicable).

title: Nostro Account Reconciliation Adjustment
description: Correcting an open item in the nostro account identified during the monthly reconciliation.
explanation: Nostro reconciliation identifies mismatches between the bank's internal nostro ledger and the correspondent bank's statement. Unresolved items are moved to suspense pending investigation. Aged suspense items must be escalated — they may indicate transaction errors, fraudulent entries, or timing differences.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Nostro reconciliation is a critical daily process managed in specialized reconciliation tools (AutoRek, TLM, SmartStream) or in SAP BRS (Bank Reconciliation Statement). Items unresolved beyond 3-5 days require RM escalation. In Oracle FLEXCUBE, nostro entries are matched via the 'NOSTRO RECONCILIATION' module.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: External and internal auditors focus heavily on aged suspense items. Items older than 30 days without resolution are a critical finding. Suspense credits that are not identified and returned to rightful parties are an AML risk. CBJ examinations always include a nostro/suspense reconciliation review.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Correspondent bank statement (MT950), internal nostro ledger, reconciliation report with open items, escalation memo for aged items, and resolution evidence for cleared items.

title: Overnight Interbank Lending (Money Market)
description: Lending excess liquidity overnight to another Jordanian bank at the JOIBOR rate.
explanation: Overnight lending is a key liquidity management tool. The bank earns JOIBOR minus a credit margin for overnight risk. The transaction matures the following business day. Despite the short tenor, IFRS 9 ECL (12-month, Stage 1) technically applies.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In SAP TRM or Oracle FLEXCUBE MM, overnight interbank deals are entered as O/N (overnight) money market placements. SWIFT MT320 confirms the deal. Settlement is via CBJ's RTGS (Jordan Automated Clearing System - JACS). CBJ publishes the daily JOIBOR fixings that serve as the benchmark.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check that counterparty limits are not breached by overnight placements. CBJ large exposure limits apply even for overnight exposure. Related-party overnight placements must be at market rates and disclosed separately.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Treasury dealing ticket, SWIFT MT320, CBJ JACS settlement confirmation, JOIBOR rate fixing confirmation, and counterparty limit utilization report.

title: Reverse Repo — Securities Purchased Under Resale Agreement
description: Bank provides cash to a counterparty receiving government bonds as collateral, with agreement to resell them.
explanation: A reverse repo is a secured lending transaction — the bank lends cash and holds securities as collateral. The securities are not recognized on the bank's balance sheet (the counterparty retains risks and rewards). The bank earns the repo rate on the reverse repo receivable.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Reverse repos are managed in SAP TRM as secured lending or in Oracle FLEXCUBE MM/SY module. The collateral securities must be tracked in the bank's collateral management system even though they are off-balance-sheet. GMRA (Global Master Repurchase Agreement) governs the transaction.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the collateral (government bonds) is held in the bank's name in a segregated account at the CSD during the repo period. If the counterparty defaults, the bank must be able to liquidate the collateral within the prescribed timeframe. Haircut adequacy is tested — under-margined positions require margin calls.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: GMRA agreement, repo confirmation (MT320), CSD collateral holding confirmation, collateral valuation with haircut, and margin call records (if any).

title: Card Interchange Income — Issuing Bank Receives from Acquirer
description: Recording the interchange fee received from the acquiring bank for a cardholder purchase transaction.
explanation: The issuing bank (cardholder's bank) receives interchange from the acquiring bank (merchant's bank) for each card transaction. This compensates the issuer for fraud risk, credit risk, and customer acquisition costs. The rate is set by the card scheme (Visa/MC/JONET).

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Interchange is automatically calculated and settled by the card scheme in the batch settlement run. The settlement net amount (interchange received minus scheme fees) is posted to the bank's account by the card scheme and then reflected in the CMS-to-GL interface. Individual transaction interchange is typically not posted separately — it is settled in aggregate by the scheme.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors reconcile total interchange income to the card scheme settlement statements. The interchange rate must comply with the card scheme's published interchange fee schedules. For domestic transactions on JONET, interchange rates are regulated by CBJ.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Card scheme settlement statement, CMS interchange income report, JONET/Visa/MC interchange rate schedule, and monthly reconciliation of CMS to GL.

title: Merchant Acquiring Fee (Merchant Discount Rate) Income
description: Earning the merchant discount rate (MDR) from a merchant whose POS terminal is managed by the bank.
explanation: The MDR is the total fee charged to the merchant (e.g., 1.5% of transaction value). Out of this, the acquiring bank pays the issuing bank the interchange fee, pays the card scheme its network fee, and retains the remainder as its own revenue.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Merchant acquiring is managed in the bank's Merchant Management System (MMS) or card platform. The MDR is deducted from each batch settlement to the merchant. The net settlement (after MDR deduction) is credited to the merchant's account. Reconciliation between the MMS and GL is done daily or weekly.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify MDR rates in the merchant agreement match what is actually charged. Undisclosed MDR charges are a regulatory issue. CBJ has guidelines on maximum MDR rates for certain merchant categories. Merchant chargeback exposures must be monitored.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Merchant agreement showing MDR rate, settlement batch report, MMS-to-GL reconciliation, CBJ MDR compliance certificate, and chargeback reserve balance.

title: Card Scheme Fees Paid (Visa / Mastercard / JONET)
description: Recording monthly card scheme fees paid to Visa, Mastercard, or JONET for card network services.
explanation: Card scheme fees include transaction processing fees, assessment fees, and network access fees. They are a cost of running the card business and are recognized as incurred. They reduce the net interchange revenue earned by the bank.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Scheme fees are charged by Visa/MC via their service invoices and auto-debited from the bank's settlement account at the scheme. JONET fees are billed by the Jordan Payments and Clearing Company (JPCC). The CMS records the fee components separately for management reporting on card economics.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors reconcile scheme fee invoices to the settlement account debits. Unexplained variances may indicate unauthorized deductions or processing errors. The card business profitability analysis (interchange income net of scheme fees and fraud losses) is a key management report reviewed in the audit.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Monthly Visa/MC/JONET fee invoices, settlement account debit confirmations, CMS fee expense report, and card economics management report.

title: Chargeback Processed — Cardholder Dispute Upheld
description: Processing a chargeback where the cardholder's dispute against a merchant transaction was upheld.
explanation: When a chargeback is upheld, the issuing bank reverses the transaction on the cardholder's account and seeks recovery from the acquiring bank (which seeks it from the merchant). If recovery fails (no-recourse), the chargeback becomes a fraud loss.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Chargebacks are managed in the Card Management System following card scheme dispute procedures (Visa Dispute Resolution or Mastercard Dispute Management). Each chargeback has a reason code, time limit, and required documentation. The CMS tracks the dispute status and posts the reversal to the cardholder account.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors review the chargeback ratio (chargebacks as % of total transactions) against card scheme thresholds. Excessive chargebacks can result in scheme fines or program cancellation. Fraud-related chargebacks that cannot be recovered from merchants are written off and disclosed in the bank's fraud loss report.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Cardholder dispute form, transaction evidence (or lack thereof) from merchant, chargeback reason code documentation, scheme dispute reference number, and resolution outcome.

title: Card Fraud Loss — Unrecovered Unauthorized Transaction
description: Writing off a fraudulent card transaction that cannot be recovered from the merchant or acquiring bank.
explanation: Card fraud losses are recognized when recovery is confirmed as impossible. The chargeback receivable (created when the dispute was upheld) is written off. Card fraud is a key risk KPI monitored by the bank's Fraud Management team.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The fraud management system (typically separate from CMS) tracks fraud cases and authorizes write-offs. Fraud losses are reported separately in the P&L under 'Other Operating Expenses' or a dedicated 'Card Fraud Losses' line. Visa and Mastercard require fraud loss reporting above certain rates.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors analyze fraud loss trends and test the bank's fraud detection and prevention capabilities (3D Secure, CVV checks, velocity limits). A rising fraud loss rate may indicate control weaknesses. Adequate fraud reserves must be maintained for IFRS 9 purposes.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Fraud investigation report, chargeback dispute outcome, write-off authorization, fraud loss register, and scheme fraud reporting (Visa/MC monthly fraud data).

title: Cash Vault Overage — Count Exceeds Ledger
description: Recording an overage discovered during a cash vault count where physical cash exceeds the ledger balance.
explanation: Cash overages are suspicious — they may indicate unrecorded deposits, counting errors, or (rarely) theft attempts. The overage is initially recorded as a liability pending investigation. After investigation, it is either matched to an unrecorded transaction or transferred to Other Income.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Cash vault counts are performed daily by tellers and confirmed by vault custodians. Overages are entered in the teller system and post to the Cash Differences account automatically. Unresolved differences after 5 business days are escalated to Branch Management and Internal Audit.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors perform surprise cash counts to verify teller drawer and vault balances. Any unresolved cash differences older than 10 days are a finding. A pattern of regular small overages may indicate split transactions or undisclosed customer deposits.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Cash count sheet (signed by teller and vault custodian), branch manager investigation report, and resolution documentation (matched to transaction or transferred to Other Income).

title: Cash Vault Shortage — Count Below Ledger
description: Recording a shortage discovered during a teller drawer count.
explanation: Cash shortages are more concerning than overages and may indicate teller error or theft. The shortage is recorded as a receivable (from the teller) pending investigation. If confirmed as a loss, the amount is expensed and may be recovered from the teller's personal bond/guarantee.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Same process as overages but with opposite treatment. In some banks, tellers are held personally responsible for shortages above a de minimis threshold. HR policy and labor law (Jordan) governs whether teller shortages can be deducted from salaries — this requires written teller acknowledgment.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors track the frequency and amount of teller shortages by branch. Systematic shortages from the same teller are flagged for potential fraud investigation. Internal Audit may conduct unannounced cash counts in branches with high shortage frequency.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Cash count sheet, branch manager investigation report, teller's written acknowledgment (if responsible), HR action taken, and resolution documentation.

title: Cheque Presented for Clearing — Outward
description: A customer deposits a cheque drawn on another bank; the amount is credited pending clearance.
explanation: Cheques presented for clearing are provisionally credited to the customer's account but held in a clearing suspense until the paying bank confirms payment. The suspense is cleared when the clearing cycle confirms honor or return. Provisional credits are restricted until clearance.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Cheque clearing in Jordan is processed through the Jordan Automated Clearing House (JACH). In Oracle FLEXCUBE, 'CLTD' transaction handles outward cheque presentation. The clearing cycle typically takes 1-2 business days. The customer can only withdraw the funds after the clearing suspense is cleared.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that customers cannot draw against provisional cheque credits before clearance (no kiting risk). Returned cheques (NSF) must trigger immediate reversal of the provisional credit. Outstanding clearing suspense items older than 3 business days require investigation.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Original cheque, deposit slip, JACH batch submission confirmation, and clearing outcome notification.

title: Cheque Returned — Insufficient Funds (NSF)
description: Processing a returned cheque where the paying bank has rejected it due to insufficient funds in the drawer's account.
explanation: When a cheque is returned NSF, the provisional credit to the depositor's account is reversed. The bank charges a returned cheque fee to the depositor. In Jordan, the paying bank is required to report returned cheques to CBJ — serial returned cheque drawers face criminal penalties.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE, the JACH return notification triggers automatic reversal of the clearing credit. A returned cheque fee is applied per the schedule of charges. In SAP Banking, the return event is processed via the payment return workflow. The CBJ requires banks to submit monthly returned cheque statistics.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check that returned cheques are reversed within the JACH clearing cycle timeframe. Any interest or fees credited to the customer based on a provisional cheque credit (not yet cleared) must be reversed on the cheque return. CBJ returned cheque reporting accuracy is tested.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: JACH return notification, account reversal confirmation, returned cheque fee billing, customer notification, and CBJ returned cheque report submission.

title: Outward Remittance Fee (Retail Transfer Abroad)
description: Charging a fee for processing a retail customer's international money transfer.
explanation: The bank charges a fixed or percentage-based fee for executing an international transfer. The fee is recognized at the point of transfer execution (IFRS 15 point-in-time). Correspondent bank charges may be additional and are disclosed as either SHA (shared) or OUR (sender pays all).

practitioner_notes.erp_application: In Oracle FLEXCUBE FT, outward remittances generate SWIFT MT103 messages. The fee is charged per the schedule of charges in the product definition. For OUR option transfers, correspondent bank charges are estimated and pre-deducted. AML screening must clear before the SWIFT message is sent.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: CBJ AML regulations require all international transfers above JOD 10,000 to be reported. Wire transfer fees must comply with CBJ's retail banking fee guidelines. Auditors verify that AML screening was completed before transfer execution and that beneficiary information is complete (SWIFT compliance with FATF standards).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Customer transfer instruction, AML screening clearance, SWIFT MT103 confirmation, fee billing advice, and CBJ AML reporting (for transfers above threshold).

title: Inward Remittance — Corridor Fee / Conversion Income
description: Recording an inward remittance from abroad and earning a currency conversion spread.
explanation: On inward remittances, the bank earns a FX spread by converting at a rate slightly less favorable than the interbank mid rate. The JOD 20 spread is the bank's income on the conversion. Remittance corridors (GCC-Jordan) are a major revenue source for Jordanian banks.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Inward remittances are received via SWIFT MT103 and credited to the beneficiary's account after AML and sanctions screening. In Oracle FLEXCUBE FT, 'FTTRONL' handles inward transfers. The FX conversion uses the bank's prevailing buying rate for the currency.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: CBJ AML regulations require suspicious inward transfers to be reported immediately via the goAML system. Auditors check that all inward remittances from high-risk jurisdictions are subjected to enhanced due diligence. FX rates applied must be within CBJ's permitted spread from the official rate.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: SWIFT MT103 (received), OFAC/sanctions screening clearance, goAML suspicious transaction report (if applicable), AML monitoring system clearance, and FX conversion rate confirmation.

title: Loan Commitment Fee (Undrawn Facility)
description: Charging a commitment fee on the undrawn portion of an approved credit facility.
explanation: Commitment fees compensate the bank for holding capital against an undrawn facility. Under IFRS 9 / IFRS 15, commitment fees are part of the EIR calculation if they are likely to result in a drawn loan. If the facility is not drawn, they are recognized over the facility period.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Commitment fees are accrued quarterly in the loan management system. In Oracle FLEXCUBE CL, commitment fee accrual is part of the undrawn line management. In SAP CML, the commitment fee schedule is set in the facility contract. If the facility is drawn, the previously collected commitment fee is included in the EIR calculation.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check whether commitment fees are correctly included in the EIR for drawn loans. Fees that are functionally origination fees (not true commitment fees) must be deferred. The distinction is important because early inclusion in EIR vs. straight-line recognition over the undrawn period can materially affect income timing.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Facility agreement specifying commitment fee rate, quarterly accrual calculation, billing advice, and EIR calculation showing inclusion/exclusion of commitment fee.

title: Arrangement / Syndication Fee Received (Lead Arranger)
description: Receiving a one-time arrangement fee for structuring and syndicating a large corporate loan.
explanation: Arrangement fees for the lead arranger's own participation are deducted from the loan balance (EIR method). Fees for services to participating banks (distribution and structuring advisory) may be recognized upfront if distinct from the lending service. Careful bifurcation is required under IFRS 15.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Arrangement fees are complex to account for because they may cover multiple services: (1) structuring (recognized upfront), (2) distribution to participants (recognized at successful syndication), and (3) the bank's own loan origination (deferred via EIR). Many banks use a manual Excel model to split fees into these components before posting to the GL.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: This is a high-value audit area. Auditors require a detailed fee bifurcation analysis for each syndicated deal. Fees incorrectly classified as 'arrangement income' (immediate P&L) rather than 'origination fees' (EIR deferred) overstate income. IFRS 15 requires the bank to identify distinct performance obligations.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Mandate letter specifying fee components, fee bifurcation analysis memo, legal counsel sign-off on fee structure, cash receipt confirmation, and revenue recognition timing analysis per IFRS 15.

title: Loan Agency Administration Fee Income
description: Earning ongoing agency fee for administering a syndicated loan facility as the agent bank.
explanation: The agent bank earns a quarterly fee for administering the syndicated loan: collecting repayments from borrower, distributing to participants, managing information flow, and enforcing covenants. This is a continuous service (over-time recognition under IFRS 15).

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Agency fees are managed separately from the agent bank's own participation in the loan. In Oracle FLEXCUBE SY (Syndications), agency fee billing is automated per the agency agreement. In SAP CML, a separate contract for the agency role is set up with its own fee billing schedule.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors confirm the agency fee is recognized over the agency service period (quarterly or annually), not upfront. If the agency agreement terminates early, any unearned fee must be returned. The agent bank must also confirm it has no conflicts of interest (holding significant own participation alongside the agency role).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Agency agreement, quarterly fee billing advice, agency function activity report, and reconciliation of agency fee income to active syndicated facilities.

title: Collective ECL Provision — Statistical Model (Portfolio Level)
description: Running the month-end ECL model on the total performing loan portfolio to update the collective provision.
explanation: The collective ECL provision covers the entire performing loan portfolio using a statistical model. The net movement (increase or decrease in the provision) is recognized in P&L. This is distinct from individual (Stage 3) provisions which are calculated case-by-case.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The collective ECL model typically runs outside the core banking system (in a risk modeling platform or Excel model fed by a CBS data extract). Results are uploaded back to the CBS/GL as a month-end journal entry. Oracle OBCL and SAP Credit Risk Analyzer can host the model calculations natively for banks with advanced implementations.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: External auditors perform model validation annually and test key assumptions (PD by segment, LGD by collateral type, EAD factors for undrawn commitments, macroeconomic overlay). CBJ examiners compare the bank's ECL coverage ratio against industry peers and challenge outliers.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: ECL model technical documentation, monthly model run output, macro-economic overlay approval (ALCO/BRC minutes), sensitivity analysis, independent model validation report, and reconciliation of ECL balance movement to P&L.

title: ECL Macro-Economic Overlay — Management Adjustment
description: Applying a management overlay to the model-based ECL to reflect emerging macro-economic risks not captured in historical data.
explanation: Macro-economic overlays (also called 'post-model adjustments') are management judgments applied on top of the statistical ECL model to capture risks not yet reflected in historical data (e.g., new sanctions, sector concentration risk, geopolitical events). They are critical for IFRS 9 compliance.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Overlays are purely manual management decisions documented in the ECL Overlay Committee minutes and posted as separate GL entries from the statistical model output. The overlay amount and rationale must be fully documented and approved by the Chief Risk Officer and reviewed by the Audit Committee.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Macro overlays are among the most scrutinized areas by external auditors and CBJ inspectors. Auditors challenge the basis for the overlay — it must be forward-looking, specific, and not double-counted with the model. Overlays that offset model-driven provisions (negative overlays) are particularly challenged.
