practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that the pooled fund sub-ledger reconciles to the total fund balance. Each donor must be able to receive an accurate statement of their individual account. Commingling pooled fund assets with general operating funds is a compliance violation.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Pooled fund agreement (governance, investment policy, distribution policy), individual donor contribution records, pro-rata income allocation schedule, periodic donor statements, and annual fund performance report.

title: How to Write Off a Grant Receivable When the Grantor Fails to Pay
description: Writing off a previously recognized grant receivable when the grantor defaults on a committed grant.
explanation: If a previously recognized grant receivable becomes uncollectible, it is written off as a bad debt expense in the period the loss is confirmed.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Before writing off, exhaust all recovery options: formal demand letter, escalation to the board, legal counsel, and donor relationship management intervention. Document the write-off decision with evidence of the grantor's default. The write-off is a current-period expense — the original grant revenue recognized is not reversed.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors require documentation of collection efforts before accepting a write-off. A grant receivable written off without evidence of collection attempts suggests premature write-off. For government grant receivables, the default of a government grantor is unusual — auditors will scrutinize these closely and may require legal opinions.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Original grant agreement and award letter, collection correspondence (demand letters, follow-up emails), grantor's non-payment confirmation or cancellation notice, management authorization for write-off, bad debt expense entry, and any insurance or guarantee claims.

title: How to Record Direct Program Supply Purchases for Beneficiary Distribution
description: Expensing educational materials, food kits, or medical supplies purchased for direct distribution to beneficiaries.
explanation: Direct program supplies are expenses in the period they are distributed to beneficiaries, classified under the specific program they serve.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: If supplies are purchased and immediately distributed, expense on purchase. If held in inventory before distribution, record as inventory first (asset) and expense when distributed. Maintain a distribution log showing items, quantities, beneficiary names or numbers, and distribution date. This log is required for both grant accountability and beneficiary verification.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that supplies recorded as distributed to beneficiaries actually reached the intended recipients. Distribution logs with beneficiary signatures are the primary evidence. Large supply purchases at grant end with no corresponding distribution logs suggest supply diversion or fictitious spending.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Procurement invoice, delivery/receiving record, distribution log (beneficiary names or IDs, quantities, signatures), program report confirming supplies used, and inventory balance (if supplies not immediately distributed).

title: How to Record Direct Cash Transfers Disbursed to Qualifying Beneficiaries
description: Expensing cash grants distributed directly to qualifying beneficiaries as a direct program cost.
explanation: Cash transfers to beneficiaries are direct program expenses expensed when disbursed, requiring strong documentation for grant accountability.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Cash transfers require the strongest documentation of any program expense. Preferred payment methods: bank transfers (with beneficiary account numbers), mobile money (with transaction IDs), or vouchers (not cash). Maintain a complete beneficiary registry with eligibility verification. For large cash transfer programs, use a dedicated payment agent or third-party payment platform.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Cash transfer audits focus on beneficiary verification: are recipients real, verified individuals who meet eligibility criteria? Auditors may conduct field visits, cross-check with government social registries, or use biometric verification. Multiple individuals receiving transfers to the same phone number or bank account is a major red flag.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Beneficiary registration list with eligibility documentation, transfer authorization per beneficiary, payment confirmation (mobile money transaction ID, bank transfer reference), beneficiary receipt or acknowledgment, and monitoring visit report confirming transfers reached beneficiaries.

title: How to Record Beneficiary Voucher Issuance and In-Kind Distribution to Program Recipients
description: Recording the issuance of food vouchers or commodity packages to beneficiaries, with the liability cleared on redemption.
explanation: Vouchers create a liability when issued and are cleared when redeemed at partner vendors. Physical goods are expensed at cost when distributed.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: For voucher programs: create the Voucher Liability when vouchers are issued to beneficiaries; clear the liability when vendors submit redemption claims; expense as Program Expense at redemption. For in-kind goods: expense from inventory at cost on the distribution date. Maintain a voucher control register showing serial numbers issued, beneficiary, redemption status, and value.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test the completeness of voucher control — are all issued vouchers accounted for (redeemed, cancelled, or outstanding)? A voucher program where more value is redeemed than issued indicates fraud. Vendor redemption claims must be matched to beneficiary-signed vouchers.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Voucher issuance register (serial numbers, beneficiary names, values), vendor redemption claims (matched to voucher serial numbers), beneficiary-signed vouchers, unredeemed voucher tracking, physical goods dispatch and distribution records, and partner vendor reconciliation.

title: How to Record Staff Field Mission Travel, Accommodation, and Per Diem Costs
description: Expensing travel, accommodation, and per diem costs for staff on a field assessment or monitoring mission.
explanation: Field missions are direct program costs. Advances issued before travel are cleared against actual expenses upon staff return.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Issue travel advances against a documented travel authorization (approved by manager, with itinerary and budget). Upon return, the staff member submits an expense report with original receipts, clearing the advance. Per diem rates should be set in the travel policy — UN DSA rates or organizational equivalents are commonly used.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Travel advances not cleared within 30 days of return are a control issue. Auditors test that advances are cleared by expense reports with supporting documentation. Per diem rates charged above the policy rate are disallowed. Field missions with no program output may be considered unsupported costs.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Travel authorization (itinerary, budget, manager approval), travel advance record, expense report with original receipts, trip report documenting purpose and outcomes, and advance clearance confirming no outstanding balance.

title: How to Record Fuel and Maintenance Costs for Program Vehicles
description: Expensing fuel and routine maintenance for vehicles used exclusively or primarily for program activities.
explanation: Vehicles used purely for programs are a direct program cost. Shared-use vehicles require cost allocation based on mileage or usage logs.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain a vehicle logbook per vehicle showing: date, driver, destination, purpose (program/admin/personal), and odometer reading. Use the logbook to allocate fuel and maintenance costs across functional categories monthly. For shared vehicles, apply the mileage-based allocation from the logbook.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors request vehicle logbooks and cross-check fuel purchases to distance traveled. Fuel purchases without logbook support suggest either personal use being charged as program or missing documentation. Unusually high fuel costs relative to program activity level are investigated.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Vehicle logbook (date, driver, destination, purpose, odometer), fuel receipts, maintenance invoices, functional allocation calculation based on mileage, and vehicle insurance and registration confirming NGO ownership.

title: How to Record Training and Capacity Building Program Expenses
description: Expensing trainer fees, venue, materials, and participant travel for a beneficiary or partner capacity building workshop.
explanation: Capacity building is a direct program expense. Trainer fees, venue hire, materials, and participant travel are all included.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Budget training events at the component level (trainer fees, venue, materials, participant transport and accommodation) for accurate grant budget management. Collect attendance lists with signatures — these serve as both program documentation and supporting evidence for donor reporting. Calculate the cost per participant trained as a unit economics metric.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors require attendance lists for all training events to confirm the number of participants matches reported outputs. Training events with no attendance list, or the same individuals attending repeatedly without justification, are questioned. Venue hire costs must be at market rates — overpriced venues may indicate a conflict of interest.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Training event plan and budget, venue invoice, trainer contract and invoice, materials procurement record, participant attendance list with signatures, training report documenting topics covered, and cost-per-participant calculation.

title: How to Record Grant-Funded Program Equipment as a Capitalized Fixed Asset
description: Capitalizing laptops, medical equipment, or solar panels purchased with grant funds as fixed assets tracked separately.
explanation: Equipment purchased with grant funds is capitalized as a fixed asset. Donors usually require the NGO to track grant-funded assets separately and report on their status.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Tag each grant-funded asset in the fixed asset register with the grant name, donor, acquisition date, and asset location. Some donor agreements specify that equipment reverts to the donor at project end or must be transferred to a local partner — note any disposition requirements. Conduct annual physical verification of grant-funded assets.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Donors often conduct physical asset verification during project reviews. Missing assets (lost, stolen, or sold without authorization) require immediate reporting and may constitute a grant violation. Auditors verify that the asset register matches the physical assets and that any disposals were donor-approved.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Equipment procurement documentation, grant agreement asset provisions, fixed asset register entry (with grant tag), annual physical verification record, insurance coverage, and donor approval for any asset disposals.

title: How to Record Monthly Depreciation on Program Equipment as a Program Expense
description: Recording the monthly depreciation charge on equipment used for program delivery as a direct program cost.
explanation: Depreciation of program assets is classified as a program expense to ensure the full cost of program delivery is captured in functional expense reporting.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Assign each program asset to the program it supports in the fixed asset module. The monthly depreciation automatically posts to Program Expense. Include program depreciation in grant budget proposals so donors understand the full cost of program delivery. For IAS 20 grant-funded assets, depreciation is matched by a corresponding grant income release.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that depreciation is allocated to the correct functional category. Equipment used for multiple programs requires allocation across programs. Equipment listed as program-only that is actually used for administrative purposes will be reclassified, incorrectly inflating the program expense ratio.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Fixed asset register with program assignment, monthly depreciation schedule, functional allocation basis for shared equipment, IAS 20 deferred income release schedule (for grant-funded assets), and physical asset location record confirming program use.

title: How to Record Monitoring and Evaluation Costs as a Direct Program Expense
description: Paying for independent monitoring visits, data collection surveys, and program evaluations required by donors.
explanation: M&E is a required grant expense for most institutional donors and is classified as a direct program cost since it supports evidence of impact.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Budget M&E as a specific line item in all grant budgets — typically 5–10% of total project costs for institutional donors. M&E expenses include: evaluation consultant fees, survey tools (Kobo, ODK), data analysis, field data collection, and the final evaluation report. Classification as program expense is correct because M&E directly supports evidence-based program delivery.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test that M&E activities described in grant proposals are actually conducted and documented. An M&E line item claimed in the financial report with no corresponding evaluation reports, baseline/endline data, or monitoring visit records is unsupported. M&E must be genuinely independent — self-assessed monitoring alone may not satisfy some donor requirements.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: M&E plan from the grant proposal, evaluation consultant contract, monitoring visit reports, baseline and endline survey data, final evaluation report, and M&E budget vs. actual analysis.

title: How to Record a Donor-Required Project-Specific Audit as a Program Expense
description: Expensing an audit mandated and funded by the donor for a specific project as a direct program cost.
explanation: When a donor mandates and funds a project audit, the cost is a direct program expense charged to that grant. The fee may be partially recoverable as an indirect cost.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Project audits are included in the grant budget as a direct cost. Manage the procurement process (request for proposals, selection of audit firm) per both the NGO's and donor's procurement policies. Provide the auditor with all grant documentation. The audit report must be submitted to the donor within the required timeframe.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: The auditor conducting the project audit will examine all transactions charged to the grant. They are independent of the statutory auditor and may have different findings. A qualified project audit report must be disclosed to the donor immediately. Non-submission within the required timeframe is a grant compliance breach.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Donor grant agreement specifying audit requirement, audit firm selection documentation, engagement letter, project audit report, and donor submission confirmation.

title: How to Record Monthly NGO Staff Payroll Allocated Across Program, Management, and Fundraising
description: Recording gross salaries for all NGO staff with the correct functional allocation across program, management and general, and fundraising.
explanation: NGOs must allocate payroll across functional categories for the Statement of Functional Expenses, based on time sheets or activity-based estimates.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The allocation must be based on actual time use — time sheets are the gold standard. For staff who work on a single program full-time, direct-charge to that program. For shared staff (e.g., the Finance Manager who supports multiple grants and M&G), use a time-based allocation updated quarterly. Program salaries are typically the largest component of grant expenditure and must reconcile to the grant budget.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Salary allocations are tested against time sheets or documented activity records. Auditors spot-check allocations across at least two periods to confirm consistency. Program staff whose entire salary is claimed on a single grant while actually working on multiple programs is an over-allocation finding. Time sheet signatures from both the employee and supervisor are required.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Time sheets per employee (hours by activity, employee signature, supervisor signature), functional allocation table by employee, payroll register, SSC and EOSB accruals allocated consistently, grant budget reconciliation for salaries, and quarterly allocation review.

title: How to Accrue Monthly EOSB for NGO Staff in Jordan Across Functional Categories
description: Building the statutory end-of-service gratuity liability for Jordanian NGO staff, allocated across program and management.
explanation: EOSB is allocated across functional categories like salaries. The provision ensures the liability is built gradually rather than creating a large unexpected cost when an employee leaves.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Apply the same functional allocation split used for salaries to EOSB. The EOSB provision per employee is calculated monthly using current gross salary. For grant-funded staff, include EOSB in grant budgets — many NGOs fail to budget EOSB and face cash flow problems when long-serving staff leave. Review the Provision for EOSB annually to confirm it covers all staff entitlements at current salary levels.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: EOSB provisions are tested for completeness (all staff included) and accuracy (current salary rate, correct service months). The EOSB provision is a significant liability for NGOs with tenured field staff — understating it inflates net assets. Auditors may require external actuarial validation for large, long-serving staff populations.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: EOSB calculation per employee (start date, current salary, months of service, provision amount), payroll records confirming current salaries, Provision for EOSB reconciliation, functional allocation schedule, and grant budget review confirming EOSB is included.

title: How to Record the Employer SSC Contribution for NGO Staff in Jordan Across Functional Categories
description: Recording the employer's 14.25% Social Security contribution for all Jordanian NGO staff, allocated proportionally across program and management.
explanation: SSC is allocated proportionally across functional categories. The employer share is part of the true cost of employment and must be reflected in grant budgets.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Apply the same allocation percentages as salaries to SSC contributions. Include the employer SSC cost in all grant budgets — underbidding on staff costs (excluding SSC) is a common budgeting error that leaves the NGO covering the cost from unrestricted funds. Remit to the SSC by the 15th of the following month with employee contributions.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: SSC compliance is tested by the Social Security Corporation, which can audit NGOs. All staff (including expat staff if employed locally) must be enrolled from their first working day. SSC contributions on commissions and overtime must be included in the insurable salary base. NGOs are not exempt from SSC obligations.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Monthly SSC calculation per employee, SSC Form 4 submission, SSC payment receipt, functional allocation schedule, employee SSC enrollment certificates, and grant budget confirming SSC is included.

title: How to Record an Expat Staff Housing Allowance as a Program Staff Cost
description: Paying the monthly housing allowance for an international staff member stationed in Jordan.
explanation: Housing allowances for expat staff are a program staff cost. They must be included in grant budgets as they are a significant donor-scrutinized cost.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Housing allowances must be defined in the employment contract and the NGO's compensation policy. Budget housing allowances in all grant proposals for expat positions — many donors cap housing at a specific rate (e.g., UN housing rates for the duty station). Compare actual housing costs to the donor cap and recover only the allowable amount from the grant.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Donors and auditors scrutinize expat costs as some of the highest-value items on grant budgets. Housing amounts above the donor's published ceiling rates require pre-approval. Payments to staff-owned accommodation is a related-party transaction requiring board approval and arms-length pricing. Housing must be for the duty station, not vacation properties.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Employment contract specifying housing allowance, donor ceiling rate comparison, lease agreement for the staff member's accommodation, payment records, board approval for related-party arrangements, and grant budget line confirmation.

title: How to Reimburse Volunteers for Meals and Transportation During Program Activities
description: Reimbursing volunteers for out-of-pocket meal and transport costs incurred while supporting NGO program work.
explanation: Out-of-pocket reimbursements to volunteers are a legitimate program expense subject to the same approval controls as staff expenses.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Require volunteers to submit expense claims with original receipts. Set reimbursement limits per the NGO's volunteer expense policy (aligned with staff travel policy). Pay by bank transfer or mobile money where possible — cash reimbursements require signed receipts. Track volunteer reimbursements by activity to assess the true cost of volunteer-supported programs.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Volunteer reimbursements without receipts may be disallowed by donors. Large reimbursements to volunteers who are also NGO employees (dual role) require careful examination to ensure they are genuine volunteer costs, not disguised salary payments. Volunteer costs used as cost-share require signed volunteer time sheets.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Volunteer expense claim form with original receipts, volunteer activity confirmation, reimbursement authorization, payment record, and volunteer activity report confirming program contribution.

title: How to Record a Consultancy Contract Payment for Technical Expertise on a Program
description: Paying an external consultant for specific technical deliverables on a grant-funded project.
explanation: Consultants provide specific technical skills for defined deliverables. Their fees are a direct program cost. Withholding tax obligations apply in Jordan.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Use a written consultancy contract for every engagement regardless of amount. The contract should specify: deliverables, timeline, daily rate, total fee, and payment schedule. Pay upon delivery of agreed outputs — milestone-based payments are preferred. In Jordan, withholding tax (5% for residents, higher for non-residents under certain conditions) must be deducted from consultancy payments.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test that consultants are genuinely independent (not disguised employees). An exclusive, long-term arrangement where the consultant works full-time only for the NGO with fixed hours and NGO-provided tools may be reclassified as employment — creating payroll tax and SSC liabilities. The deliverable-based contract and evidence of independence are key defenses.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Consultancy contract (scope, deliverables, rate, timeline), CV confirming qualifications, deliverable report or output confirming work was done, payment authorization, bank transfer confirmation, withholding tax deduction and remittance records, and independence certification.

title: How to Record a Staff Redundancy or Severance Payment When a Grant Ends
description: Recording a lump-sum severance payment when a position is eliminated due to grant funding ending, drawing against the EOSB provision.
explanation: When a grant ends, positions are often eliminated. The EOSB provision covers part of the payment; the excess above the provision is an additional expense in the termination period.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Calculate the total payment: EOSB entitlement (per Jordan Labor Law formula) plus any contractual notice pay. The EOSB provision absorbs the accrued entitlement; any additional contractual severance above the provision is an additional expense. Negotiate with active donors to include redundancy costs in grant budgets — end-of-grant staff costs are a real and often overlooked liability.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the termination entitlement calculation against the Labor Law and employment contract. The total payment (provision + additional expense) must reconcile to what was actually paid. The employee should sign a final settlement agreement (waiver of further claims) — absence of this document creates an open liability.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Termination notice, EOSB entitlement calculation (Labor Law formula), notice pay calculation, final settlement agreement signed by the employee, bank transfer confirmation, EOSB provision balance prior to use, and any donor reimbursement for redundancy costs.

title: How to Record the Purchase of an Investment for the Endowment Portfolio
description: Investing endowment cash in a diversified portfolio of stocks and bonds per the Investment Policy Statement.
explanation: Endowment cash is invested to generate returns. The investment is restricted — it remains in the endowment fund. Only the income it generates is available for spending.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain the endowment's investment portfolio in a separate fund in the ERP, clearly segregated from operating assets. Record each investment at cost, then update to fair value at each reporting date. Classify investments per ASC 820 / IFRS 13 fair value hierarchy (Level 1: quoted prices; Level 2: observable inputs; Level 3: unobservable). Investment decisions must follow the board-approved IPS.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors confirm that endowment investments are properly authorized by the board's investment committee and consistent with the IPS. They obtain independent confirmation of investment values from the custodian. Commingling endowment and operating investments in the same brokerage account without a sub-account structure is a segregation control failure.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Investment Policy Statement, investment committee authorization, brokerage trade confirmation, investment register by security (cost, FMV, unrealized gain/loss), custodian account statement, fair value hierarchy classification, and performance report vs. benchmark.

title: How to Record an Endowment Investment Sale for Portfolio Rebalancing
description: Selling a portion of the endowment portfolio to rebalance asset allocation, recognizing the realized gain.
explanation: Investment rebalancing exchanges one asset for another. Realized gains remain restricted within the endowment unless the board appropriates them for spending.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Calculate the realized gain/loss as sale proceeds minus the specific lot cost (FIFO or specific identification per the investment policy). The gain remains within permanently restricted net assets unless the donor agreement or applicable law permits realized gains to be treated as temporarily restricted income available for spending. Rebalancing decisions must be authorized by the investment committee.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the cost basis used to calculate the realized gain. The cost method must be consistent with the investment policy and prior periods. Realized gains on permanently restricted endowments must remain restricted unless specifically permitted to be distributed.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Investment committee rebalancing authorization, trade confirmation (securities sold, quantities, proceeds), cost basis calculation (specific lot or FIFO), realized gain/loss calculation, updated investment register, and net asset classification of the gain.

title: How to Record Interest Income Earned on Endowment Fixed-Income Investments
description: Recognizing interest earned on bonds or fixed deposits held within the endowment portfolio.
explanation: Interest on endowment investments is restricted — it stays within the endowment fund unless the board appropriates it for operations.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Endowment income (interest, dividends) accumulates in the restricted fund until the board adopts the annual spending distribution. Record income as With Restrictions unless the donor agreement specifies otherwise. The investment manager or custodian typically provides monthly income statements — reconcile to the ERP monthly.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that endowment income is classified correctly (restricted or temporarily restricted) based on the donor agreement and applicable state law. Income spent outside of the board-approved spending distribution without authorization is a compliance failure.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Bond interest schedule or bank deposit interest statement, custodian monthly income statement, interest income entry matched to bank receipt, net assets with donor restrictions roll-forward, and board spending distribution authorization.

title: How to Record Dividend Income Received on Endowment Portfolio Equity Holdings
description: Recording dividends paid on stocks held within the endowment investment portfolio.
explanation: Dividends received by the endowment accumulate within the fund until the board decides on the annual spending distribution.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Record dividends when received (cash dividends) or declared (for accrual purposes). Like interest income, dividends remain restricted within the endowment until the board's spending appropriation. The annual total investment return (interest + dividends + realized gains + unrealized gains) is the basis for the spending distribution calculation.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors check that return-of-capital distributions (which reduce the investment cost basis, not income) are not misclassified as dividend income — this would overstate income and understate the investment's cost basis.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Custodian dividend statement or broker confirmation, distinction between income dividends and return-of-capital distributions, cash receipt, dividend income entry in restricted net assets, and annual total return calculation.

title: How to Record a Realized Gain When Endowment Stocks Are Sold Above Cost
description: Recognizing a capital gain on the sale of endowment portfolio securities sold above their original cost.
explanation: Realized gains on endowment investments remain restricted within the endowment unless the board appropriates them for spending per the spending policy.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The realized gain is the difference between sale proceeds and the cost basis of the specific lot sold. Classify as With Restrictions (permanently or temporarily depending on donor agreement and jurisdiction). Under UPMIFA, realized gains on true endowments are generally treated as part of the endowment fund — not available for operations until appropriated. Update the investment register to remove the sold securities.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the cost basis calculation and confirm the gain is correctly classified. They also check whether the sale was authorized by the investment committee and consistent with the IPS. Unreported realized gains (netting against losses to show only the net) are not permitted — gross gains and losses must be disclosed separately.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Investment committee sale authorization, trade confirmation (securities sold, proceeds, date), cost basis lot record, realized gain calculation, investment register update, and net asset classification (restricted).

title: How to Record a Realized Loss When an Endowment Investment Is Sold Below Carrying Value
description: Recording a capital loss when endowment securities are sold below their carrying value, reducing the endowment's net assets.
explanation: Losses reduce the endowment's net asset balance. Persistent losses can make an endowment 'underwater' — where fair value falls below the original gift amount.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Realized losses are classified against permanently restricted net assets, reducing the endowment's balance. When cumulative losses bring the endowment's fair value below the original historic dollar value of the gift, the endowment is 'underwater.' An underwater endowment has specific accounting treatment and disclosure requirements and may restrict the spending distribution.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors assess whether any endowments are underwater and whether the required disclosure is included in the financial statements. Continuing to make spending distributions from an underwater endowment may violate donor agreements and UPMIFA. Investment decisions that led to underwater status are a governance concern.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Investment committee sale authorization, trade confirmation, cost basis record, realized loss calculation, investment register update, underwater endowment assessment (fair value vs. historic dollar value), and if underwater: disclosure and spending policy adjustment documentation.

title: How to Record the Annual Endowment Spending Distribution Transfer to Operations
description: Transferring the board-approved annual spending amount from the restricted endowment fund to the unrestricted operating fund.
explanation: The board authorizes an annual spending rate (typically 4–5% of endowment value). The transfer releases cash from the restricted endowment to the unrestricted operating account.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The spending distribution must be authorized by a board resolution specifying the amount and calculation methodology (e.g., 5% of the trailing 36-month average endowment market value). Document the calculation and board approval before transferring. The transfer simultaneously moves cash between bank accounts (restricted to operating) and releases the net asset restriction.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the spending distribution against the board-approved spending policy and the endowment agreement. Distributions exceeding the authorized rate or made without board approval are compliance violations. The calculation of the spending base (trailing average) must be accurate.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Board resolution authorizing the annual spending distribution, spending rate calculation (trailing average method), endowment agreement confirming distribution is permitted, bank transfer confirmation between accounts, net asset release entry, and annual endowment performance report.

title: How to Establish a Board-Designated Quasi-Endowment from Unrestricted Reserves
description: Recording the board's designation of unrestricted reserves as a quasi-endowment fund.
explanation: A quasi-endowment is created from unrestricted funds by the board — unlike true endowments, the board can undesignate it at any time.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Quasi-endowments remain legally unrestricted (without donor restrictions) — the board can undesignate them at any meeting. Distinguish clearly in financial reporting between quasi-endowments (board-designated, within 'Without Donor Restrictions') and true endowments (With Donor Restrictions). Present them separately in the net assets section and note disclosure.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Quasi-endowments must NOT be presented as 'restricted' because they are legally available to the board at any time. Presenting a quasi-endowment alongside donor-restricted endowments would mislead readers about the organization's true financial flexibility.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Board resolution establishing the quasi-endowment (amount, investment objective, undesignation conditions), net asset roll-forward showing the designation, note disclosure explaining the nature of quasi-endowments, investment policy, and annual board review.

title: How to Record a Periodic Annuity Payment Made to a Charitable Gift Annuity Donor
description: Making the contractual periodic payment to a donor who established a Charitable Gift Annuity, reducing the annuity liability.
explanation: Each annuity payment reduces the liability recognized at the CGA's inception. Upon the donor's death, the remaining liability balance becomes unrestricted.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain a payment schedule per CGA showing: donor name, payment amount, frequency, next payment date, and remaining liability balance. Automate payments via standing order to the donor's bank account. At each reporting date, remeasure the liability (reduced for payments made and for the donor's increasing age reducing remaining life expectancy). Upon the donor's death, the remaining liability is released to unrestricted revenue.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the annuity payment schedule against the gift annuity agreement and test that all payments have been made on schedule. They also check the remeasurement of the liability at the reporting date. The liability release upon death requires a death certificate and estate documentation.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Charitable gift annuity agreement, annuity payment schedule, bank transfer confirmations per payment, annual liability remeasurement calculation, death certificate and liability release entries (at termination), and actuarial report for large CGA portfolios.

title: How to Capitalize the Purchase of Office Equipment for the NGO Headquarters
description: Recording the purchase of computers, printers, and office furniture above the capitalization threshold as fixed assets.
explanation: Equipment over the capitalization threshold is a fixed asset. The cost is allocated between Management & General and Program based on how the equipment is used.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set a capitalization threshold (e.g., JOD 200 per item or JOD 1,000 for computer sets) — items below this are expensed immediately. Items above the threshold are capitalized and depreciated over their useful life (computers: 3 years; printers: 3–5 years; furniture: 5–7 years). Tag each asset with a unique asset number and physical label. Annual physical verification of all equipment is required.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors perform physical asset verification — they will inspect equipment in the office and field offices against the asset register. Missing or mislocated assets require investigation. Equipment purchased with grant funds must be tracked under the grant asset register. Assets disposed of must be derecognized promptly.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Procurement invoice, delivery receipt, fixed asset register entry (asset number, description, cost, useful life, location), annual physical verification record, insurance coverage, and functional allocation of depreciation.

title: How to Record Monthly Depreciation on Office and Program Fixed Assets
description: Recording monthly depreciation across all fixed assets used by the NGO.
explanation: Depreciation is allocated across functional categories based on how each asset is used. This ensures the Statement of Functional Expenses reflects the true cost of delivering programs versus running the organization.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Run the fixed asset depreciation module monthly. Ensure each asset profile is mapped to the correct functional department (Program vs. Management & General) so the ERP automatically splits the expense upon posting.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors will review the fixed asset register and recalculate depreciation to ensure adherence to the NGO's capitalization policy and stated useful lives. Incorrect functional allocation of administrative assets to programs is a common audit finding.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Fixed asset register, monthly depreciation schedule, functional allocation mapping, and capitalization policy.

title: How to Record Subsequent Depreciation for a Donated Fixed Asset
description: Depreciating a vehicle that was donated and recorded at fair value.
explanation: Donated assets are depreciated the same way as purchased assets — starting from the recorded fair value. A vehicle worth JOD 8,000 with a 5-year life generates JOD 133/month of depreciation.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set the asset up in the ERP at its appraised Fair Market Value (FMV) as of the donation date. Run standard straight-line depreciation against this base value over the asset's estimated useful life.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors will trace the depreciation base back to the independent FMV appraisal from the gift date. They verify that the useful life assigned matches standard policies for that asset class, regardless of how it was acquired.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: FMV appraisal from the gift date, fixed asset register entry, and monthly depreciation journal.

title: How to Capitalize Leasehold Improvements for an NGO Program Office
description: Capitalizing fit-out costs for a rented program office.
explanation: Permanent improvements to rented space are capitalized and depreciated over the shorter of the lease term or useful life. For an NGO, these are typically program or management expenses.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Create a 'Leasehold Improvements' asset class. When capitalizing fit-outs, calculate the depreciation period carefully: use the remaining lease term (including highly probable renewals) or the physical useful life of the improvement, whichever is shorter.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors will examine the office lease agreement. If an improvement is depreciated over 10 years but the lease expires in 3 years with no renewal clause, the depreciation schedule will be flagged for accelerated write-off.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Office lease agreement, contractor invoices for fit-out, capitalization threshold memo, and asset creation record.

title: How to Record a Construction Draw and Release Capital Campaign Restrictions
description: Using restricted capital campaign funds to pay a construction contractor.
explanation: As capital campaign funds are spent on the building, the restriction is released. The cash decreases and the CIP asset increases. Restrictions are released in proportion to spending.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Process the contractor invoice against the 'Construction in Progress' (CIP) account. Simultaneously, trigger a net asset release journal to move the equivalent amount from restricted to unrestricted net assets, showing donors the funds were used for the specified purpose.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test the restriction release against contractor progress billings. They ensure restricted capital cash is maintained separately and that no CIP funds are inappropriately diverted to cover general operating deficits.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Architect's progress certification, contractor invoice, bank transfer from restricted account, and net asset release schedule.

title: How to Write Off and Dispose of a Fully Depreciated Fixed Asset
description: Removing a fully depreciated computer or printer that is no longer in use.
explanation: When an asset is fully depreciated and disposed of, both the cost and accumulated depreciation are removed. No gain or loss arises if the asset has zero book value.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Use the ERP's asset disposal module. Select 'Scrap' or 'Retire' with zero proceeds. This automatically clears the historical cost and accumulated depreciation balances without hitting the P&L.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: During physical asset verification, auditors look for 'ghost assets' — items on the register that have been discarded. The disposal must be formally authorized to ensure assets weren't stolen or sold off-books.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Asset disposal authorization form signed by management, e-waste or scrap handover receipt, and updated fixed asset register.

title: How to Record a Grant-Funded Asset as Deferred Income Under IAS 20
description: Recording a government grant received to buy program equipment as deferred income.
explanation: Under IAS 20, grants for assets are deferred and recognized as income over the same period the asset is depreciated. Each month, a portion of the deferred grant income is released to match the depreciation expense.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Create an amortization schedule for the Deferred Grant Income liability that perfectly mirrors the asset's depreciation schedule. Many modern ERPs can link a deferred income account to an asset profile to automate the matching monthly release.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors will verify IAS 20 compliance by comparing the monthly depreciation expense against the grant revenue release. The net effect on the P&L should be zero. If the asset is sold or scrapped early, the remaining deferred income must be released immediately.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Grant award letter, asset purchase invoice, deferred income amortization schedule, and monthly matching journal entries.

title: How to Perform a Month-End Net Asset Reconciliation for an NGO
description: Verifying that the three net asset classes (Unrestricted, Temporarily Restricted, Permanently Restricted) balance.
explanation: This is a reconciliation check entry, not a transaction. The CFO or Finance Manager verifies that the sum of all three net asset classes equals total assets minus total liabilities at month-end.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Generate a Trial Balance and a Statement of Financial Position. Ensure that the retained earnings/net assets carry-forward plus current year surplus/deficit across all fund codes mathematically equals total Assets minus total Liabilities. Resolve any out-of-balance fund codes immediately.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Fund accounting systems can easily become unbalanced if an inter-fund transfer is one-sided or a revenue/expense is booked without a fund code. Auditors review the net asset roll-forward as a primary test of system integrity.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Month-end Trial Balance by fund, Statement of Financial Position, and Net Asset roll-forward schedule.

title: How to Release Net Assets from a Time-Based Donor Restriction
description: Releasing a time-restricted donation when the specified time period has arrived.
explanation: Some donors specify that funds may only be used after a certain date. When that date arrives, the time-restriction is automatically lifted with this reclassification entry.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain a calendar or tracking module for time-restricted pledges. On the date specified by the donor, post a journal entry to release the restriction. No cash moves; this is purely an equity reclassification.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test time restrictions by comparing the release date in the GL to the date explicitly stated in the donor's pledge letter. Prematurely releasing a time-restricted asset inflates unrestricted net assets.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Donor pledge letter explicitly stating the time restriction, time restriction tracking calendar, and the net asset release journal.

title: How to Record a Prior Year Net Asset Misclassification Correction
description: Correcting an error where a restricted grant was incorrectly recorded as unrestricted.
explanation: Net asset misclassifications from prior periods are corrected by adjusting the opening balances. If material, this may require restating prior year financial statements.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Do not post this to current year revenue or expense. Adjust the opening balances of the respective net asset accounts. Ensure the adjustment is clearly tagged as a prior period correction for audit trail visibility.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors heavily scrutinize any adjustments to opening retained earnings/net assets. If the misclassification is material, it triggers a 'Prior Period Restatement' disclosure in the audited financials, explaining the nature of the error.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Management memo detailing the error discovery, board or audit committee authorization for the adjustment, and restated comparative financials.

title: How to Record Foreign Currency Translation Adjustments for a Field Office
description: Translating a field office's monthly activity from USD to JOD for consolidation.
explanation: Field offices report in their local currency. At consolidation, exchange rate differences between the transaction date and reporting date create a cumulative translation adjustment recorded in net assets.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Use the ERP's consolidation module. Apply the average exchange rate for P&L items (revenue/expense) and the month-end spot rate for balance sheet items. The resulting imbalance is posted automatically to the Cumulative Translation Adjustment (CTA) account in equity.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors will recalculate the translation using published central bank rates. They check that the CTA is properly classified in net assets and not incorrectly mixed into realized/unrealized P&L gains and losses.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Field office local currency trial balance, central bank exchange rate printouts, and the ERP translation calculation report.

title: How to Record a Bank Reconciliation Adjustment for Interest Earned
description: Adjusting the general ledger for interest income appearing on the bank statement.
explanation: Bank interest is unrestricted income unless the board has placed restrictions on specific accounts. It is recognized when it appears on the bank statement during reconciliation.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: During the monthly bank reconciliation process, post adjusting entries for any bank-originated transactions (interest earned, bank fees) before locking the period. Code interest to unrestricted revenue unless the account holds strictly restricted funds where the donor agreement claims interest.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors review bank reconciliations for stale, unresolved items. Unrecorded interest or fees are a sign of sloppy month-end close procedures. They also verify if grant agreements require interest earned on grant advances to be returned to the donor.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Monthly bank statement, completed bank reconciliation report signed by the preparer and reviewer, and grant agreement checks for interest-return clauses.

title: How to Accrue a Provision for Outstanding NGO Grant Commitments
description: Accruing the estimated future expenditure committed under active grant agreements.
explanation: NGOs with signed grant agreements have future spending obligations. Provisioning at year-end ensures the financial statements reflect the full cost of existing commitments.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Assess signed sub-grant agreements and major contracts at year-end. If an unconditional obligation exists where the NGO cannot avoid payment, accrue the liability. Conditional commitments (where payment relies on future milestones) are typically disclosed in the notes rather than accrued.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors heavily scrutinize this area to distinguish between true liabilities (unconditional promises) and mere commitments. Over-accruing provisions to 'burn' budget at year-end is a major compliance violation.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Sub-recipient grant agreements, milestone achievement reports, year-end commitment assessment memo, and note disclosures.

title: How to Accrue the Annual Statutory Audit Fee at Year-End
description: Accruing the auditor's fee at year-end before the invoice is received.
explanation: The annual audit relates to the fiscal year just ended. Accruing the fee ensures the expense is matched to the period being audited, not the following year when the invoice arrives.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Post the accrual as part of year-end closing entries based on the signed engagement letter. Code entirely to Management & General unless specific grant rules allow a portion to be direct-charged as project audit fees.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors perform a search for unrecorded liabilities. They expect to see their own fee accrued in the year they are auditing. Failure to accrue the audit fee is a basic cut-off error.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Signed audit engagement letter specifying the fee, and year-end accrual schedule.

title: How to Record the Annual NGO Registration and License Renewal Fee
description: Paying the annual renewal fee to the Ministry of Social Development or relevant authority.
explanation: NGO registration renewals are mandatory operating costs. They are classified under Management & General as they benefit the entire organization rather than a specific program.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Process the payment directly to the relevant ministry. Use recurring calendar reminders to ensure the fee is paid on time, as late payment can jeopardize the NGO's legal operating status.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors require proof of the NGO's legal existence and good standing. The receipt for the annual license renewal serves as primary evidence that the entity is authorized to continue operations.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Payment receipt from the Ministry, updated registration certificate, and bank transfer confirmation.

title: How to Record the Payment of an Accrued Statutory Audit Fee
description: Paying the external auditor's invoice for the annual financial statement audit.
explanation: This clears the accrued audit fee liability set up at year-end. The expense was already recognized — this is simply the cash settlement.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: When the auditor's invoice arrives, match it against the Accrued Expenses account rather than hitting the P&L again. If the final invoice differs from the accrual, record the minor difference as a current year adjustment.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors review subsequent disbursements to verify that accrued liabilities were actually settled. Lingering accruals from prior years suggest overstatement of liabilities.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: External auditor's final invoice, original year-end accrual journal, and payment remittance advice.

title: How to Record Legal and Compliance Expenses for NGO Operations
description: Paying a lawyer for reviewing grant agreements and employment contracts.
explanation: Legal fees for organizational compliance, contract review, and employment matters are Management & General expenses. Legal fees directly related to a specific program would be a program expense.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Code general retainer fees to M&G. If a lawyer is hired specifically to support beneficiary cases (e.g., a refugee legal aid program), those specific invoices must be coded to Program Expense.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors review legal expense accounts very carefully to identify potential contingent liabilities, lawsuits, or regulatory investigations that management may not have disclosed.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Lawyer's invoice detailing services provided, legal engagement letter, and board minutes discussing any material legal matters.

title: How to Record the Payment of Unrelated Business Income Tax (UBIT)
description: Paying the Unrelated Business Income Tax accrued in a prior period.
explanation: This clears the UBIT liability recognized when the income was earned. The payment is made to the tax authority — in Jordan, to the ISTD.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Ensure the payment matches the exact liability calculated on the tax return. Process the payment via the designated banking channel to the tax authority to avoid late penalties.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors will vouch the payment to the filed tax return. Failure to pay UBIT can result in penalties, interest, and severe risks to the NGO's overall tax-exempt status.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Filed UBIT tax return, tax authority payment receipt, and bank settlement confirmation.

title: How to Record Withholding Tax Deducted from Foreign Grant Receipts
description: Recording withholding tax deducted by a foreign donor before disbursing a grant.
explanation: Some bilateral donors are required to withhold a percentage before disbursing. The NGO recognizes the gross grant as revenue. The withholding is a tax expense unless recoverable under a tax treaty.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Record the grant revenue at the gross award amount. Code the withheld amount to a tax expense account. If the NGO is eligible to reclaim the tax under a double taxation treaty, code it to a 'Withholding Tax Receivable' asset instead.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the gross-up calculation. If the WHT is recorded as a receivable, auditors will test the recoverability assessment; if it is unlikely to be recovered from the foreign tax authority, it must be written off to expense.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Grant award letter, foreign donor's withholding tax certificate, bank receipt showing net amount, and tax treaty analysis if claiming as a receivable.

title: How to Record a VAT-Inclusive Purchase for a Tax-Exempt NGO
description: Recording a purchase where the NGO cannot reclaim VAT due to its exempt status.
explanation: NGOs with tax-exempt status cannot reclaim input VAT. The full amount including VAT is expensed or capitalized. This is different from commercial entities where VAT is a recoverable asset.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Configure supplier tax codes in the ERP as 'Non-Recoverable.' This ensures the system automatically absorbs the VAT amount into the total expense or asset cost line rather than routing it to a VAT Receivable account.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the NGO's official tax-exempt status. They will check that no VAT receivable balances are lingering on the balance sheet, as the NGO has no mechanism to recover them from the tax authority.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Supplier tax invoice showing the VAT amount, NGO tax-exempt certificate, and ERP tax configuration settings.

title: How to Record the Annual Filing Fee to an NGO Regulatory Authority
description: Paying the annual reporting and filing fee to the NGO regulatory authority.
explanation: Annual filing fees are a standard compliance cost for registered NGOs in Jordan. They are classified as Management & General since they benefit the whole organization.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Record under Management & General. Track filing deadlines meticulously, as missing the annual filing window often triggers immediate fines and restricts the NGO's ability to receive foreign funding approvals.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors confirm that all annual returns and associated fees have been filed. Non-compliance indicates poor governance and threatens the going concern status if operations are suspended by regulators.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Ministry receipt, copy of the submitted annual report/return, and evidence of board approval for the submission.

title: How to Record Advance Ticket Sales for a Fundraising Gala as Deferred Revenue
description: Recording advance ticket sales for an annual fundraising gala.
explanation: Ticket sales before the event are deferred — the performance obligation (providing the event experience) has not yet been met. Revenue is recognized on the night of the event.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set up a specific liability sub-account for the event (e.g., 'Deferred Revenue: Annual Gala 2026'). Process all early ticket sales, sponsorships, and table purchases into this account. Do not recognize any P&L revenue yet.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors perform cut-off testing around event dates. Recognizing ticket sales as revenue before the event occurs is a common error that overstates current period income and understates liabilities.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Ticket sales platform reports, bank deposit slips, event budget, and deferred revenue schedule.

title: How to Recognize Deferred Ticket Revenue and Expenses on Gala Event Night
description: Recognizing ticket revenue and recording event costs on the night of the gala.
explanation: On event night, deferred revenue converts to earned revenue. Direct costs (venue, catering, entertainment) are expensed simultaneously to show the net fundraising proceeds.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Once the event concludes, post a journal to clear the Deferred Revenue liability to Special Event Revenue. Ensure all vendor invoices for the event are accrued to 'Fundraising Expense' in the same period to accurately calculate the net event margin.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test that revenue is recorded gross (not netted against expenses). The portion of the ticket price representing the fair market value of the meal/entertainment must be disclosed to donors for their personal tax deductions.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Event completion memo, final ticket sales reconciliation, vendor invoices, and donor tax acknowledgment letters outlining the exchange portion.

title: How to Record Net Proceeds and Fees from an Online Crowdfunding Campaign
description: Recording net proceeds from a GoFundMe or LaunchGood crowdfunding campaign.
explanation: Crowdfunding platforms deduct their fees before disbursing. Gross donations are recorded as revenue and the platform fee is a fundraising expense. Revenue classification depends on whether the campaign specifies a purpose.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Never record just the net cash received. Always pull the platform's financial report, gross up the revenue to the total amount donors gave, and record the withheld amount as a fundraising fee. Classify as restricted if the campaign promised funds to a specific cause.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Netting revenue against platform fees violates GAAP/IFRS gross reporting principles. Auditors will request access to the crowdfunding platform dashboard to verify the gross numbers match the general ledger.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Crowdfunding platform payout report showing gross donations and fees, bank settlement statement, and the campaign's public page to verify any donor restrictions.

title: How to Record Peer-to-Peer Fundraising Payouts as Contribution Revenue
description: Receiving funds raised by individual volunteer fundraisers on behalf of the NGO.
explanation: P2P fundraisers collect donations on the NGO's behalf. The funds are recognized as contributions when received by the NGO. The fundraiser acts as an agent — their collections are the NGO's revenue.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set up a specific revenue code for P2P campaigns to track their effectiveness. Integrate the P2P platform with your CRM to ensure the individual donors (not just the volunteer fundraiser) receive appropriate tax receipts and stewardship.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test the 'variance power' principle. Since the volunteer fundraiser is raising money explicitly for the NGO and cannot redirect it elsewhere, the NGO must recognize the revenue fully. Receipts must go to the original donors, not the volunteer.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: P2P platform settlement report, CRM data import log, and donor acknowledgment letters.

title: How to Record Donor Stewardship and Recognition Expenses
description: Recording costs of donor recognition events, impact reports, and thank-you gifts.
explanation: Donor stewardship costs (annual reports, thank-you events, impact visits) are classified as fundraising expenses. They are essential for donor retention but must be monitored as a percentage of fundraising revenue.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Code strictly to Fundraising Expense. Do not attempt to reclassify stewardship events as 'Program' or 'Education' to artificially lower the fundraising ratio. Track cost-per-dollar-raised closely.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors aggressively test expenses coded to Program to ensure they are not disguised fundraising costs. Sending impact reports to existing donors is considered a fundraising/stewardship activity, not a public education program.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Vendor invoices, donor event attendee lists, sample stewardship materials (reports, letters), and functional expense allocation checks.

title: How to Record Ticket Refunds Due to a Fundraising Gala Cancellation
description: Refunding ticket holders when an event is cancelled.
explanation: If the event is cancelled, the deferred revenue liability is cleared by refunding ticket holders. No revenue is recognized since the performance obligation will not be fulfilled.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Reverse the balance out of the specific Deferred Revenue sub-account. Issue refunds via the original payment method. If a ticket holder tells the NGO to 'keep the money as a donation,' process a journal moving their specific amount from Deferred Revenue to Contributions Revenue.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors will verify that all deferred revenue tied to a cancelled event is cleared. They will test a sample of the refunds to ensure the cash actually returned to the donors, preventing misappropriation.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Event cancellation board memo, refund transaction logs, bank statements showing outgoing transfers, and written communications from any donors opting to convert their ticket to a donation.

title: How to Record Corporate Sponsorship Revenue as an Exchange Transaction
description: Recording a corporate sponsor's payment for naming rights or event sponsorship.
explanation: If the sponsor receives something in return (logo placement, speaking slot), it is an exchange transaction — not a contribution. It is recognized as revenue when the benefit is delivered.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Review the sponsorship contract. If it's pure advertising (exchange), recognize revenue when the event occurs. If it's a mixed transaction (e.g., $10k paid, but advertising value is only $2k), split the entry: $2k to Exchange Revenue, $8k to Contribution Revenue.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors test the bifurcation of sponsorships. Pure exchange sponsorships might trigger Unrelated Business Income Tax (UBIT) exposure if the sponsor's business is heavily promoted (beyond a simple logo acknowledgment).
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Corporate sponsorship agreement detailing benefits provided, fair market value assessment of the advertising/benefits, and bifurcated revenue journal.

title: How to Record Ticket Sales and Prize Expenses for a Charity Raffle
description: Recording ticket sales from a charity raffle event.
explanation: Raffle proceeds are fundraising revenue. The cost of prizes is a fundraising expense. Net proceeds flow to the program or general fund. Local gaming/lottery laws must be observed.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Record ticket sales gross. Do not net the prize costs against the revenue. Ensure strict cash handling controls are in place during ticket sales, using pre-numbered tickets to reconcile total cash expected versus cash banked.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Charity raffles are heavily regulated. Auditors verify that the NGO obtained the necessary permits from local authorities. They will reconcile the number of tickets sold against the cash deposited to detect skimming.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Government charity lottery/raffle permit, pre-numbered ticket log, cash count sheets signed by two individuals, prize purchase receipts, and winner acknowledgment forms.

title: How to Capitalize the Cost of a 3D Seismic Survey as an Exploration and Evaluation Asset Under IFRS 6
description: Capitalizing a 3D seismic survey conducted during the exploration phase as an E&E asset.
explanation: Under IFRS 6, exploration and evaluation expenditures may be capitalized as E&E assets. Seismic surveys generate data about subsurface geology and are a direct exploration cost. The policy choice to capitalize or expense must be consistent and disclosed.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Set up a dedicated E&E asset class in the fixed asset module with sub-accounts by license block or exploration area. Tag each seismic survey cost to the specific license area to support impairment testing at the CGU level. Track the survey contractor invoices against the approved exploration budget. The E&E asset balance is reviewed at each period-end for impairment indicators — budget overruns, licence expiry approaching, or a decision to abandon are key triggers. Maintain a separate sub-ledger for seismic data costs vs. well costs to facilitate impairment testing per IFRS 6.18.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify that the exploration licence was in place at the time the seismic survey was conducted — capitalizing seismic costs before licence acquisition is not permitted under IFRS 6. They also test whether the company's accounting policy (capitalize or expense E&E costs) is consistently applied. Significant seismic programs may require an updated reserve or resource estimate to support the carrying value of the E&E asset.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Executed exploration licence confirming rights over the block, seismic survey contractor agreement, contractor invoices with field data acquisition dates, seismic data processing and interpretation report, exploration budget approval, and period-end E&E asset impairment assessment.

title: How to Capitalize Exploratory Drilling Costs as an E&E Asset Pending Reserve Determination
description: Capitalizing the cost of drilling an exploratory well to test the presence of hydrocarbons, pending commerciality assessment.
explanation: Exploratory wells are drilled to test if oil or gas is present. The cost is capitalized pending determination of whether commercially viable reserves exist. If reserves are confirmed, the cost is reclassified to development; if not, it is written off.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Record all exploratory well costs (day-rate drilling contractor, mud and chemicals, well logging, casing, cementing, completion testing) to the E&E asset sub-account for that specific well. Use a project code structure by well name. Track against the approved well AFE (Authorization for Expenditure). The capitalized balance must be reviewed at each reporting date — if the well has been drilled more than 12 months without a commerciality determination, enhanced disclosure is required under IFRS 6 and the asset faces heightened impairment risk.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors focus on the 'one-year rule' for suspended exploratory wells — costs can only remain capitalized beyond 12 months if (a) sufficient reserves have been found to justify completion and (b) management is actively making the commerciality assessment. They will request a timeline of management deliberations for any well suspended beyond one year. The well status report (drilling results, core/log analysis, reserve estimate) is the primary supporting document.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Well AFE (Authorization for Expenditure) approved by management and partners, daily drilling report, well completion report and mud log, wireline log interpretation, reservoir engineering assessment of discovered volumes, Management's commerciality assessment (updated at each reporting date for suspended wells), and partner joint interest billings.

title: How to Write Off a Dry Hole Exploratory Well When No Commercial Reserves Are Found
description: Writing off the full cost of an exploratory well after it is determined to contain no commercially viable hydrocarbons.
explanation: A dry hole is an exploration failure. When a well proves non-commercial, all associated E&E costs must be written off immediately. This is one of the highest-risk aspects of oil & gas accounting — explorers may write off many wells before finding a commercial discovery.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The write-off is triggered by the management decision to abandon the well — typically evidenced by a Well Operations Report confirming no commercial quantities. Process the write-off in the period the decision is made, not when the well is physically plugged and abandoned (P&A). Maintain a separate Dry Hole Expense line on the income statement for transparency. The write-off is immediate and full — no partial write-down is permitted. Update the exploration dashboard showing cumulative dry hole costs vs. discoveries to date.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Delayed dry hole write-offs are one of the most common earnings management risks in E&P. Auditors will test whether the company has a documented decision date for abandoning the well and whether that date matches the write-off period. Management communications (Board papers, partner notifications, competent person reports) are key evidence. For wells suspended beyond 12 months, the presumption shifts toward write-off unless active commerciality assessment is documented.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Well Abandonment Decision paper (Board or investment committee sign-off), geological/geophysical assessment confirming no commercial reserves, Competent Person's Report or independent reserve assessor opinion, well completion report confirming formation evaluation results, partner notification of dry hole status, and plugging and abandonment plan.

title: How to Reclassify an E&E Asset to a Development Asset After Commercial Viability Is Confirmed
description: Reclassifying an exploratory well from an E&E asset to a development asset (PP&E) when technical and commercial viability is established.
explanation: Once a discovery is confirmed as technically and commercially viable, the E&E asset is reclassified to PP&E or intangible assets depending on the nature of the rights. Depletion commences when production begins.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: The reclassification is triggered by management's formal determination of commercial viability — typically documented in a Field Development Plan (FDP) or Investment Decision paper. Upon reclassification, the asset moves from the E&E sub-class (IFRS 6) to PP&E or intangibles (IAS 16/IAS 38) and becomes subject to IAS 36 impairment testing rather than the IFRS 6 impairment rules. From this point, all additional development costs (development wells, production facilities, pipelines) are added to the Development Assets account. Depletion using the Units of Production (UOP) method commences when the field is brought into production.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: Auditors verify the date of the commerciality determination against the reclassification date — the reclassification must occur in the period the decision is formally made. They will also confirm that the FDP or investment decision is approved at the appropriate governance level (Board or investment committee) and that proved developed reserves have been recognized by a Competent Person. After reclassification, the asset is subject to annual IAS 36 impairment testing.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: Field Development Plan (FDP) or investment decision paper approved by the Board, Competent Person's Report confirming proved reserves, reservoir engineering volumetric assessment, partner approval of the development plan, and updated impairment assessment under IAS 36 post-reclassification.

title: How to Test and Record an E&E Asset Impairment When Indicators Arise Under IFRS 6
description: Writing down an E&E asset when facts and circumstances suggest the carrying amount may exceed the recoverable amount.
explanation: IFRS 6 requires E&E assets to be tested for impairment when facts and circumstances suggest the carrying amount may exceed the recoverable amount — e.g., licence expiry approaching, no plans to develop, or the area is being relinquished.

practitioner_notes.erp_application: Maintain an E&E asset register organized by licence block with expiry dates flagged for advance review (typically 12 months before expiry). At each reporting date, assess each block against IFRS 6 impairment indicators: (a) licence period is expiring and renewal is not expected, (b) no further E&E expenditure is budgeted for the area, (c) E&E in the area has not led to discovery and the company has decided to discontinue, or (d) sufficient data exists to assess commerciality but the project is not commercially viable. If any indicator is present, perform a full impairment test. The E&E CGU for impairment is typically the individual exploration block.
practitioner_notes.audit_triggers: E&E impairment is a high-risk area because management has significant discretion over the assessment of commerciality. Auditors will examine board papers, budgets, and management communications to identify E&E assets where impairment indicators exist but no impairment has been recorded. Licence expiry dates approaching within 12 months without active renewal discussions are particularly scrutinized. Auditors may also request an independent geological assessment to validate the E&E asset carrying value.
practitioner_notes.required_documentation: E&E asset register with licence expiry dates, exploration budget for the upcoming period by block, geological assessment of the block's prospectivity, licence renewal status (correspondence with the host government), management's written assessment of impairment indicators per block, and any independent Competent Person's Report.

title: How to Capitalize Drilling and Completion Costs for a Development Well in a Proven Field
description: Capitalizing the full cost of drilling and completing a development well as part of the oil and gas property.
